entry.summary: Balanced Fair Division and Generalized Kneser Graphs arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies allocating indivisible goods to two prescribed nonempty groups whose members have arbitrary monotone valuations. entry.title: Near-MMS fair allocations when few extra agents are present
entry.summary: Almost-MMS allocations with small agent redundancy arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies fair allocation of indivisible goods, asking whether a subset of n agents among more agents can each receive at least a fixed fraction of their n-maximin share (MMS). The authors show that when agent redundancy is positive, this fraction approaches 1 as n grows. This also holds without redundancy when the number of goods is at most (2−c)n. Adapting their techniques, they improve a result of Ezra and Garbuz, showing that without redundancy, n−O(log²n) agents can always receive their full MMS. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show that with agent redundancy the MMS fraction tends to 1 as n grows, yielding a corollary for m≤(2-c)n and improving Ezra and Garbuz's result.

entry.title: Fast Equilibrium Computation for the Colonel Blotto Game
entry.summary: Efficient Equilibrium Computation in Colonel Blotto Games arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies Colonel Blotto, a resource-allocation game where two players split budgets across battlefields and the higher allocation wins each battlefield's value. It gives a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme that computes an epsilon-Nash equilibrium in time polynomial in the input length and 1/epsilon. For sufficiently balanced budgets and battlefield values, it also computes exact equilibria in linear time. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme for equilibria in Colonel Blotto games, plus linear-time exact equilibria for balanced cases.

entry.title: Tight Bound for Randomized Truthful Scheduling
entry.summary: Tight Analysis of Randomized Truthful Scheduling: An (m+1)/2 Lower Bound arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies randomized truthful mechanisms for minimizing makespan on unrelated machines. It proves a lower bound of (m+1)/2 on the approximation ratio for truthful-in-expectation mechanisms, determining the optimal ratio as m/2 plus a constant. It also raises the leading constant of the lower bound for universally truthful mechanisms from 3/2−√2 to 1/2, which together with a known upper bound settles that ratio up to lower-order terms. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a (m+1)/2 lower bound for randomized truthful makespan scheduling, improving the leading constant from about 0.0858 to 1/2.

entry.title: Tight limits for fair-in-expectation job scheduling on machines
entry.summary: Sharp Bounds for Truthful-in-Expectation Scheduling arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies randomized mechanisms that schedule indivisible jobs on n unrelated machines, where each selfish machine owner privately knows its job processing times. The mechanisms are truthful in expectation and aim to minimize the expected makespan. For n of at least 7, the authors prove the optimal approximation ratio is (n+1)/2, and they give a matching mechanism. For two machines the optimal ratio is about 1.505995705434, and for three machines it is 2. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a matching lower and upper bound of (n+1)/2 for n≥7 and exact constants for two and three machines, for truthful-in-expectation scheduling.

entry.title: Constant-factor fair-share guarantees for subadditive valuations
entry.summary: Toward Constant-Factor Maximin Share Guarantees for Subadditive Valuations arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies maximin share (MMS), a fairness measure for dividing indivisible goods among n agents. For general subadditive valuations, it improves the known guarantee from Ω(1/log log n) to Ω(1/log* n). It also introduces q-partitioning valuations, an intermediate class between subadditive and XOS, and proves constant guarantees when q/n has a positive lower bound. For XOS valuations, the universal guarantee rises from about 0.2353 to 0.3125. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the general subadditive MMS guarantee exponentially to Ω(1/log* n) and report constant guarantees for intermediate q-partitioning valuation classes.

entry.title: Computational Complexity of Continuous Contract Design over Polymatroids
entry.summary: The Complexity of Continuous Contract Design over Polymatroids arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies optimal contracts where an agent allocates continuous effort under polymatroid capacity constraints. Linear costs admit polynomial-time computation of an optimal contract, while for quadratic costs the agent's best response is computable but optimizing the principal's share is NP-hard. The authors show an optimal quadratic-cost contract always exists with a share at most 1/2, which yields approximation schemes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show NP-hardness and exponentially many breakpoints for quadratic-cost contracts over polymatroids, and prove a share of at most 1/2 suffices for approximation.

entry.title: Distributed graph computation that survives node crashes
entry.summary: Local Distributed Computation under Crash Failures arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies deterministic algorithms for locally checkable graph problems in the synchronous LOCAL model, where crashing nodes may send messages to only some neighbors. The authors introduce consistent neighborhoods, which let a fault-free T-round algorithm be simulated locally and remain correct on subgraphs. The paper gives upper and lower bounds on the number of rounds needed to build these views, and reports complexity results for LCL problems and sinkless orientation under crashes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce consistent neighborhoods for crash-tolerant LOCAL simulation, reporting near-tight upper and lower bounds plus LCL complexity separations.

entry.title: Randomized fair allocation of chores with a few disposals, guaranteeing a near-maximin-share standard
entry.summary: Best-of-Many-Worlds MMS Allocation for Chores with Sublinear Disposals arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies randomized (lottery-based) allocations of indivisible chores under additive costs. It introduces MMS1, a fairness notion requiring each agent's bundle to meet the maximin share bound after removing at most one chore. The main result shows that every instance admits an ex-ante proportional lottery whose every allocation is MMS1, with all but o(n) agents satisfying MMS. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce MMS1 and report ex-ante proportional lotteries where nearly all agents get MMS, improving known chore-allocation fairness bounds.

entry.title: Logarithmic comparison queries for fair item allocation
entry.summary: Logarithmic Comparison-Query Complexity for EF1 Allocations arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies how many comparison queries are needed to find an allocation of indivisible items among n agents that is envy-free up to one item (EF1). Algorithms may only ask which of two bundles an agent prefers, never seeing numerical values. The authors give algorithms using O(log m) queries for every fixed n≥2, matching a known Ω(log m) lower bound. The results cover both chores with nonnegative costs and goods with nonnegative valuations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve an open question, giving O(log m) comparison-query EF1 algorithms for every fixed n≥2, matching the known lower bound.

entry.title: A paper showing self-stabilising approximate clock synchronisation needs linear time
entry.summary: Self-stabilising approximate clock synchronisation requires linear time arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies clock synchronisation in distributed systems where processes may start in arbitrary states and up to f processes may suffer non-transient faults. The authors prove that deterministic self-stabilising approximate clock synchronisation tasks require Ω(f) time to stabilise, giving the first non-trivial time lower bound for these tasks. The result shows that tolerating both transient and non-transient faults is costly even for approximate synchronisation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove the first nontrivial Ω(f) time lower bound for self-stabilising approximate clock synchronisation, using a topological argument.

entry.title: Lower bounds for adaptive relaxed locally decodable codes
entry.summary: Lower Bounds for Adaptive Relaxed Locally Decodable Codes via the Capped Horvitz--Thompson Estimator arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proves a nearly optimal lower bound on the blocklength of general relaxed locally decodable codes (RLDCs), extending prior results to nonlinear encodings and adaptive decoders with two-sided error. It shows that any q-query RLDC must have blocklength n = k^{1+Ω(1/q)}, closely matching a known upper bound. The proof reduces the problem to estimating the output distribution of adaptive decoders, using a capped Horvitz–Thompson estimator with bounded discrete derivatives on the p-biased cube. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors extend RLDC lower bounds to nonlinear encodings and adaptive two-sided-error decoders, obtaining a nearly tight n=k^{1+Ω(1/q)} bound via a capped Horvitz–Thompson estimator.

entry.title: Distributed LTL Synthesis under Arbitrary Message Adversaries
entry.summary: Distributed LTL Synthesis under Arbitrary Message Adversaries arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how two processes communicating in rounds over unreliable links can be automatically given distributed programs that satisfy linear temporal logic specifications, even though at least one message is delivered each round. It shows that this synthesis is undecidable in general, even when messages carry complete causal histories. The authors characterize exactly which communication restrictions, modeled as message adversaries, make synthesis decidable. For omega-regular adversaries, synthesis is decidable if and only if the image of the adversary's histories in the unit interval is nowhere dense. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a complete characterization of decidable distributed LTL synthesis under message adversaries, linking it topologically to repeated bounded-time consensus.

entry.title: Computational Difficulty of Exact Autobidding Equilibria
entry.summary: On the Complexity of Exact Autobidding Equilibria arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how hard it is to compute autobidding equilibria, which link advertisers' value multipliers or participation probabilities through aggregate budget and ROI constraints. It establishes the exact computational complexity of finding these equilibria in several canonical settings, including second-price ROI pacing and budget- or ROI-constrained generalized second-price sponsored shopping. It also analyzes the complexity of approximating the equilibrium control vector when the target accuracy is given as input. ★★★★ Notable: The authors establish FIXP-completeness of exact autobidding equilibrium computation across several canonical settings, a new complexity characterization relevant to computational economics.

entry.title: EvoCG: A self-evolving precision-control method that speeds up conjugate gradient solvers
entry.summary: EvoCG: Self-Evolving Precision Control for Faster Conjugate Gradient arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents EvoCG, a mixed-precision conjugate gradient solver that uses a reinforcement-learning policy to choose precision for each tile during iteration. It is supported by a Tile-CSC mixed-precision SpMV kernel and a low-overhead in-loop runtime. Tested on 47 SPD matrices, it reports geometric-mean speedups over several baseline solvers and a time-to-solution gain over an FP64 version at the cost of more iterations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors treat tile-wise precision as online RL control within CG iterations, co-designed with a mixed-precision SpMV; reported 1.9–7x geometric-mean speedups across 47 SPD matrices.

entry.title: Binary Huffman coding with unequal letter costs is NP-complete
entry.summary: Binary Huffman Coding with Unequal Letter Costs Is NP-Complete arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies optimal binary prefix coding when letters have unequal costs. The authors prove that deciding whether a binary prefix-free code with frequency-weighted cost at most a given threshold exists is NP-complete, even when the letter costs are consecutive positive integers (M, M+1) given as input. The proof uses two polynomial-time reductions starting from Planar Independent Set. The result implies that finding an optimal code is NP-hard. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove NP-completeness of binary Huffman coding with unequal letter costs, via two polynomial-time reductions from Planar Independent Set.

entry.title: Plotkin-optimal pure quantum LRCs with large minimum distances from NMDS codes
entry.summary: Plotkin-optimal pure quantum LRCs with large minimum distances from NMDS codes arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents a general framework for building optimal pure quantum locally recoverable codes (qLRCs) that reach a Plotkin-like bound, using Hermitian dual-containing near maximum-distance separable (NMDS) codes. It focuses on extended subcodes of generalized Reed-Solomon (ESGRS) codes, determining their localities by analyzing subset sum problems over finite fields. Using the algebraic structure of these codes, the authors construct four families of such qLRCs with large lengths and more flexible minimum distances than existing constructions.

entry.title: Computing Distortion in Social Choice
entry.summary: Computational Aspects of Distortion arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies the distortion framework in social choice theory, which measures the efficiency of randomized selection of an alternative based on agents' preferences. The authors present a linear-programming algorithm that computes the optimal randomized decision for a given instance, which is simpler and faster than prior methods. They also give a non-convex quadratic programming algorithm to compute the exact distortion of any randomized positional scoring rule.

entry.title: Parallel Python implementation of sparse nonlinear dynamics identification (SINDy) using Numba, OpenMP, threads and multiprocessing, tested on Lorenz and Rössler systems
entry.summary: Parallel Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics in Python: Task- and Data-Parallel SINDy with Numba, OpenMP, Threads and Multiprocessing for the Lorenz and Rössler Systems arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents an open-source Python implementation of SINDy, a method that recovers interpretable governing equations from time-series data by sparse regression. The same loop-based kernels are compiled with Numba and run on a shared-memory multicore node through four interchangeable back ends: Numba prange, OpenMP via PyOMP, Python threads, and multiprocessing with shared memory. On the Lorenz and Rössler systems, all back ends recover the exact sparsity pattern, reach 14.8 to 20.3 speed-up on 24 cores, and cut total time to solution by up to 117 times relative to PySINDy.

entry.title: What Limits Serving Speed in Looped Language Models: Measurements and Optimizations Ranked by Exactness
entry.summary: What Sets the Serving Speed of Looped Language Models? Measurements and Optimizations Graded by Exactness arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper measures how fast two looped language models, Ouro and Huginn-0125, can be served in an open-source inference engine. Because these models reuse the same block of layers many times per token, per-layer overhead is paid on every loop. The authors rank their optimizations from bitwise-identical changes to those requiring an accuracy check, and report throughput gains alongside effects on GSM8K accuracy.

entry.title: A study of numerical bugs in GPU programs and automated detection
entry.summary: An Investigation on Numerical Bugs in GPU Programs Towards Automated Bug Detection arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper analyzes 397 real-world numerical bug samples from GitHub in GPU programs, identifying their root causes, symptoms, triggering input patterns, test oracles, and fixing strategies. The authors also present GPU-NBDetect, a preliminary tool that detects numerical bugs across six bug categories. It found 226 bugs in 186 mathematical functions across four libraries, and developers confirmed 60 of them.

entry.title: Computer-aided design and checking of cheat-proof facility placement on distance networks
entry.summary: Search and Verification for Strategyproof Facility Location on Metric Graphs arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies how to automatically design randomized facility location mechanisms on continuous metric graphs that are strategyproof, with the goal of minimizing total distance. The authors develop methods for computing upper and lower bounds on the best approximation ratio achievable by such mechanisms, and introduce finite representations called piecewise-linear attributions. Certified upper and lower bounds are computed on several metric graphs.

entry.title: Analysis of Serverless Workloads Across Function-as-a-Service Platforms
entry.summary: Characterizing Serverless Workloads: A Large-Scale Analysis of Function-as-a-Service Platforms arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper compares eight publicly available Function-as-a-Service workload traces from major cloud providers and a scientific computing platform. It characterizes invocation patterns, latency, cold start behavior, and resource utilization. The authors report that execution times have shortened, shifting bottlenecks toward platform scheduling and dependency management, and that concurrent long-lived containers are increasingly used. They also find resource over-provisioning and highly skewed user request volumes.

entry.title: Rank-metric intersecting codes: extending intersecting codes to the matrix rank metric
entry.summary: Rank-metric intersecting codes arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Intersecting codes are codes in which any two nonzero codewords share a common nonzero coordinate. This paper extends the notion to the matrix rank-metric setting, defining the support of a matrix as its row space. Using the slice space of the generator tensor, the authors give a geometric characterization equivalent to the intersecting property, which yields parameter bounds, one of them sharp, along with first constructions. For codes closed under multiplication, i.e. matrix algebras, the intersecting property can be read from the Jacobson radical and the socle, enabling flexible construction of many such codes.

entry.title: Short proof and generalization of the rainbow cycle theorem, with improved bounds for binary even-query LCCs
entry.summary: A Short Proof and Generalization of the Rainbow Cycle Theorem and Improved Bounds for Binary Even-Query LCCs arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies rainbow cycles, which are cycles in which no color appears more than once. It gives a short proof of an earlier result showing that a properly edge-colored graph with sufficiently large average degree always contains a rainbow cycle, and extends this to weighted graphs with list-colored edges. Using this generalization, the authors prove an upper bound on the dimension of binary linear even-query locally correctable codes, closing the gap with the best known lower bounds for odd-query codes.

entry.title: APN Property of Two Function Families over F_{2^n} from the Switching Construction
entry.summary: The APN Property of Two Families of functions over F₂ⁿ from the Switching Construction arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies whether two norm-perturbed Budaghyan–Helleseth–Kaleyski functions F_2 and F_3 over F_{2^{2m}} are APN (almost perfect nonlinear). It proves a conjecture of Helleseth, Ichanska, and Kaleyski. Using the basis (1,β), each function is shown to be EA-equivalent to a simpler function, and their derivatives reduce to two trace equations for a matrix P in GL(2,F_{2^m}). Showing that these equations have no solutions establishes that both functions are APN.

entry.title: ForgeKernel: a self-evolving system that writes GPU kernels and matches or beats experts
entry.summary: ForgeKernel: Self-Evolving Kernels Catching and Surpassing Experts and Agents arXiv · Nov 3, 2026ForgeKernel is a system that automatically writes high-performance GPU kernels and improves them across runs. It studies how a strong reference kernel behaves on hardware, turns validated design choices into reusable knowledge, and reuses kernels that pass correctness and performance checks as references for later optimization. On NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, it matches or beats an expert reference on 25 of 29 configurations, with a 10% geometric-mean gain. It also ranks highly on Ascend 910C benchmarks.

entry.title: Linear equivalence of full-weight cyclic orbit codes
entry.summary: Linear Equivalence of Full Weight Spectrum Cyclic Orbit Codes arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper classifies linear-equivalence classes within two families of full-weight-spectrum one-orbit cyclic subspace codes, answering the second open problem posed by Castello, Polverino and Zullo. For the first family the criterion is a fractional linear transformation over F_q followed by a power of the q-Frobenius map; for the second it is an affine transformation over F_{q^2} with a power of the q-Frobenius. The proofs use polynomial spaces over finite fields, the linear-isometry theorem for cyclic orbit codes, and trace duality, and they also cover parameters lying in proper subfields of the ambient field.

entry.title: TapeSAC: an automated method for managing GPU memory when training large models
entry.summary: TapeSAC: Automated, Pareto-Optimal Fine-Grained Memory Management for Large Model Training arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents TapeSAC, a system that automatically decides which activations to save and which to recompute during training of large PyTorch models, without changing the model's forward code. During the backward pass it replays only the operations needed for values autograd consumes, and a planner chooses saved tensors from measured recomputation costs under a single peak-memory limit. The authors report reduced step times on Qwen models compared with full checkpointing and hand-tuned policies.

entry.title: Geometric limits on scaling codes to LCD codes
entry.summary: Geometric Obstructions and Sharp Genus Dependence in LCD Scalings arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies the minimum pole order of a rational function that scales a given code into a Euclidean LCD code. In characteristic two, it proves a lower bound on this threshold for odd-dimensional one-point algebraic geometry codes, using alternating Gram matrices. For three-dimensional codes on Hermitian curves it gives matching upper and lower bounds, showing the leading genus term is asymptotically sharp.

entry.title: Robust Aggregation of Quantile Reports, From Median to Interval
entry.summary: Robust Aggregation of Quantile Statistics: from Median to Interval arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how to robustly combine quantile reports from several experts, such as prediction intervals and medians, under squared loss. The aim is to minimize worst-case regret relative to an omniscient Bayesian aggregator. It proposes a regularized simple average rule for prediction intervals and a corresponding rule for medians, and analyzes when each improves on a constant baseline.

entry.title: Bankruptcy Rules That Deter Overstated Claims
entry.summary: Bankruptcy Rules for Strategic Agents arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how to divide an insufficient bankruptcy estate when claimants may overstate their claims. It adds the costs of supporting true and false claims to the model and asks which cost settings lead claimants to report their true entitlements. The proportional and constrained equal awards rules cannot guarantee truthful reporting, while for two claimants the TAL-1/2 rule (the Contested Garment rule) attains the optimal range of cost settings.

entry.title: New complete complementary codes built from extended Boolean functions and permutations
entry.summary: Construction of New Complete Complementary Codes Using Extended Boolean Functions and Permutations arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a new method for constructing complete complementary codes (CCCs), which are used in wireless communication systems to reduce interference and improve spectral efficiency. The method is based on extended Boolean functions (EBFs) and allows the code set size to exceed the sequence length, overcoming a limitation of existing constructions. It also uses functions not previously found in the literature to obtain new CCCs.

entry.title: A RISC-V simulator for the Tenstorrent Tensix architecture, built from public documentation and hardware measurements.
entry.summary: A RISC-V Simulator for the Tenstorrent Tensix Architecture arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents Wolfpine, a community-developed RISC-V simulator for Tenstorrent's Tensix architecture, supporting the Wormhole and Blackhole generations and integrating with the TT-Metal software stack. It is written in pure Python and built from public documentation, open-source software, and measurements on physical hardware. An opt-in, provenance-tracked cost model adds timing fidelity, while typed event streams, per-component tracing, and timeline export help programmers find performance bottlenecks.

entry.title: Rate-distortion-perception tradeoff for Gaussian sources with limited shared randomness
entry.summary: Rate-Distortion-Perception Tradeoff for Vector Gaussian Sources with Limited Common Randomness: Exact Characterization and Approximate Universality arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how limited common randomness improves reconstruction quality under perceptual constraints, within the distortion-rate-common randomness-perception (DRCP) framework. For vector Gaussian sources under squared-error distortion and squared Wasserstein-2 perception measures, it characterizes the DRCP tradeoff, including a generalized reverse waterfilling form for globally optimal allocations. It also derives an analytical upper bound via sequential greedy allocation and establishes approximate universality through uniform performance guarantees.

entry.title: Designing AI-mediated team communication: disclosure and honest reporting trade-offs
entry.summary: Designing AI-Mediated Communication in Teams arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how a firm should design AI-assistant-mediated communication among workers whose interests may conflict. Workers privately know local conditions and preferences, while the assistant knows aggregate project conditions, and the firm discloses project information before workers report and act. The authors find that transparency improves adaptation but can undermine truthful preference reporting, and that the optimal design depends on the degree of coordination.

entry.title: FenixWalk: Adaptive Sampling for Large Dynamic Graphs on CPU-GPU Systems
entry.summary: FenixWalk: Adaptive Sampling for Large-Scale Dynamic Graphs on Heterogeneous Architectures arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents FenixWalk, a memory-efficient system for random walks on large, changing graphs. It uses an in-place Fenwick structure that supports both rejection and inverse-transform sampling without duplicating edge weights. The full graph stays in host memory, while frequently reused vertex samplers are selectively placed on the GPU, and compact walker states are transferred to reduce communication. Experiments report average speedups of 2.06x to 400.57x over existing random-walk systems.

entry.title: LeanSparse: a memory-efficient serving system for native sparse-attention LLMs
entry.summary: LeanSparse: Memory-Efficient Serving for Native Sparse-Attention LLMs arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents LeanSparse, a serving system that reduces GPU memory use when running large language models on long contexts. During prefill it streams layer histories through two reusable GPU buffers, and during decode it uses coarse-to-fine indexing that fetches original indexer keys only for candidates. Implemented in SGLang and tested on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, it supports 2.95× as many concurrent requests and 2.14× the decode throughput of HiSparse at 950K context length.

entry.title: Finite-blocklength limits for Gaussian multiple-access and broadcast channels
entry.summary: Non-asymptotic Sphere-Packing Bounds for Finite-Blocklength Scalar Gaussian Multiple-Access and Broadcast Channels arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies achievable rate regions for Gaussian multiple-access and broadcast channels when codes have finite blocklength. It proposes a volume-uniform random coding scheme that spreads codewords evenly over an n-dimensional power sphere, combined with successive interference cancellation decoding. The authors derive a closed-form achievability bound, a lower bound on average error probability, and a fourth-order asymptotic expansion. For the two-user Gaussian MAC, they also give numerical and closed-form bounds under joint nearest-neighbor decoding and compare them with existing benchmarks.

entry.title: EvoCache: Speeding Up Browser-Based Large Language Model Downloads Using Public Cache Anchors
entry.summary: EvoCache: Accelerating Browser Large Language Model Delivery with Public Cache Anchors arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents EvoCache, a browser-managed system for delivering large language models that reconstructs the publisher version a site requests from public cache anchors stored in advance by the browser. The browser selects the anchor and performs reconstruction, while the site specifies only the target. In 240 real end-to-end browser experiments, EvoCache reduced network traffic by 78.9% and page-ready time by 64.2% compared with ordinary full downloads. It also protects cross-site cache privacy by giving cache hits and misses the same response time.

entry.title: System-level performance of large-scale integrated sensing and communication networks
entry.summary: System-level performance in massive ISAC networks arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a dynamic stochastic geometry framework for modeling large-scale integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks, with base stations placed by a Poisson point process and users and sensing objects moving randomly around them. Communication is modeled with downlink queues whose service rates depend on SINR via Shannon capacity, and sensing is modeled with a Kalman filter whose noise depends on sensing SINR. The authors prove that communication and sensing metrics at a typical base station are associated, and that this association weakens as network density grows. Simulations using a ray-tracing channel model support the analysis.

entry.title: Mutual-coupling-aware joint precoding and antenna positioning for movable-antenna MU-MIMO
entry.summary: Mutual-Coupling-Aware Joint Precoding and Antenna Positioning for Movable-Antenna MU-MIMO Systems arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies a downlink multiuser MIMO system in which both the base station and users use movable antennas. The authors combine field-response propagation with a circuit-based array model to capture mutual coupling, then maximize weighted sum-rate by jointly optimizing multi-stream precoders and antenna positions. The method works in the antenna-current domain with a current-domain WMMSE framework, handles nonconvex position updates via majorization-minimization, and solves the convex subproblems with a conic ADMM algorithm. Simulations show improved weighted sum-rate over a mutual-coupling-aware fixed array and a movable-array design that ignores mutual coupling.

entry.title: Coercive at equilibrium but nowhere monotone: exact convergence certificates for learning in first-price auctions
entry.summary: Coercive at the equilibrium, monotone nowhere: exact convergence certificates for learning in first-price auctions arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies learning of Bayes-Nash equilibria in first-price auctions, whose variational operator fails every monotonicity notion. It proposes a strong but local certificate in place of monotonicity, giving an exact constant for two bidders and a radius that decays at a precise rate with bid-space size. For general priors and bidder counts, two certificates are provided, and the limit of the learners' certificate is shown in closed form.

entry.title: Estimating the generator of a matrix exponential time series
entry.summary: Estimating the generator of matrix exponential time-series arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies estimating the generator and eigenvalues of a matrix exponential time series from noisy data. It gives non-asymptotic precision guarantees for the practical genESPRIT algorithm, showing the precision does not depend on spectral spacing. In the unitary, bounded-noise case, the estimation error matches the Cramér–Rao scaling up to logarithmic factors, providing the first rigorous bounds for this problem.

entry.title: Minimizing Bottleneck Overload Risk in Edge Task Placement Under Workload Uncertainty
entry.summary: Minimizing Bottleneck Overload Risk in Online Edge Task Placement under Workload Uncertainty arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how to place tasks on finite-capacity edge servers when workloads are uncertain and only their means and variances are known. It introduces a risk ratio, the ratio of workload fluctuation to residual capacity, which bounds each server's worst-case overload probability, and minimizes the largest such ratio. The proposed Risk-Bottleneck Placement (RBP) method outperforms an expected-utilization baseline on small exact instances and in trace-derived multi-period simulations.

entry.title: LiquidCP: Splitting Attention Work from Communication in Context Parallelism
entry.summary: LiquidCP: Decoupling Attention Tasks from Communication and Kernel Boundaries in Context Parallelism arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes LiquidCP, a method for context parallelism that splits long sequences across GPUs for LLM training and inference. It uses a shared model of transfer, compute, and reduction tasks to decouple attention work from communication and kernel boundaries, with two designs: MegaRing for training and full prefill, and MegaDCP for decoding and mixed batches. On eight H100 GPUs, it reports geometric-mean core-attention speedups of 1.23x forward and 1.18x backward for MegaRing, and 1.20x for decode-only and 1.35x for mixed batches for MegaDCP.

entry.title: Beyond Compression Ratio: High-Throughput KV Compression for Disaggregated LLM Serving
entry.summary: Beyond Compression Ratio: High-Throughput KV Compression for Disaggregated LLM Serving arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines KV cache compression for disaggregated large language model serving and argues that its practical benefit depends on how efficiently the compression pipeline executes, not only on compression ratio and model quality. The authors present \system, a high-throughput KV compression data path that fuses distribution transformation and low-bit quantization into a \tilelang kernel and replaces the lossless backend with an extensible, searchable one based on \lc. The fused kernel reaches up to 5.9x speedup, and the new backend raises compression throughput from below 90 GB/s to over 500 GB/s. Across the evaluated workloads, the system reduces job completion time by up to 2.04x.

entry.title: Efficient communication scheme for combining sparse histograms across distributed users
entry.summary: Optimal Communication for Distributed Sparse Histogram Aggregation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how much communication is needed to estimate a global histogram from many users whose local histograms are sparse, under given ℓ1 distortion and failure probability constraints. The authors propose a randomized covering scheme that uses the distortion budget to represent each user's local histogram, lowering communication costs. They show the scheme is first-order optimal via a lower bound based on identifying each user's active coordinates.

entry.title: Optimal four-dimensional lattice quantizer and Voronoi-facet-based bounds
entry.summary: Optimality of the D₄ lattice quantizer arXiv · Oct 26, 2026The paper proves that the root lattice D4 is the unique four-dimensional lattice, up to similarity, that minimizes the normalized second moment. The computer-assisted proof combines classification of secondary cones, integration over Voronoi cells, and weighted sums of squares. In dimensions two and higher, comparison with circular cones yields a lower bound depending on the number of Voronoi facets, improving the sphere bound and recovering the hexagonal value in dimension two. The authors also prove Ajjanagadde's circular-cone concavity conjecture and derive the lattice case of his conjectured quantization bound. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove D4 uniquely minimizes the normalized second moment among four-dimensional lattices, via a computer-assisted proof and a new facet-based bound.

entry.title: Binary codes that fix multiple edits, using polynomial hashing and entropy recycling
entry.summary: Seed Recycling: Explicit Codes for Mixed Synchronization Errors Matching the Leading Term of the Gilbert--Varshamov Bound arXiv · Oct 11, 2026This paper presents new explicit binary codes of length n that can correct t edits, including deletions, insertions, and substitutions, which is relevant to DNA-based storage and racetrack memories. The authors first build a systematic code with a polynomial hash, using (4t+2)log n + O_t(log log n) bits of redundancy. They then introduce entropy recycling, which uses the indices of good hashes to carry information, reducing the redundancy to (2t+1)log n + O_t(log log n) bits. The paper also provides deterministic polynomial-time encoding and decoding algorithms. ★★★★ Notable: Uses polynomial hashing to build a systematic code, then recycles good hash indices to carry information, reaching (2t+1)log n redundancy for t edits, with deterministic polynomial-time encoding and d

entry.title: A paper on how constraint geometry affects solving variational inequalities
entry.summary: On the Role of Geometry in Solving Variational Inequalities arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies how the computational difficulty of variational inequalities changes when the constraint set is an ℓp ball, for every p from 1 to infinity. For any p other than 2, finding an inverse-polynomially accurate approximate solution is PPAD-complete even when the operator is affine. For p = 2, affine problems can be solved in polynomial time, while quadratic operators again yield PPAD-completeness. ★★★★ Notable: The authors map the complexity of variational inequalities over ℓp balls, extending Ye's result to non-symmetric affine operators and reporting PPAD-completeness for quadratic operators, a theoretical

entry.title: Efficient binary codes that correct edit errors at the Gilbert-Varshamov bound
entry.summary: Making Every Edit Count: Efficient Binary Edit Correction at the Gilbert-Varshamov Bound arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper constructs binary codes that reach the classical Gilbert-Varshamov redundancy guarantee for a fixed number of edit errors. For each fixed t≥1 and sufficiently large block length n, the codes correct any combination of at most t insertions, deletions, and substitutions, with redundancy at most 2t·log₂n+O_t(1). For fixed t, construction, encoding, and decoding all run in polynomial time in n, and decoding recovers the original message. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report polynomial-time constructions attaining the Gilbert-Varshamov redundancy bound for binary codes correcting up to t combined edit errors.

entry.title: Why truncation is the best linear sketch for binary data
entry.summary: On the optimality of truncation among binary linear sketches arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies inference and function evaluation when a binary input vector is accessible only through a fixed number of parity measurements, called a binary linear sketch. Under a monotonicity condition, the authors show that simply keeping a subset of coordinates is optimal among all linear sketches of the same size. This yields lower bounds for any binary linear sketch. For a distributional graph connectivity problem on n vertices, linear sketches need Θ(n log n) bits for constant error, while a nonlinear protocol needs only O(log n) bits. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show truncation is optimal among binary linear sketches under monotonicity, and report a Θ(n log n) lower bound for graph connectivity versus O(log n) nonlinear protocols.

entry.title: PhotonZip: A Lifecycle-Aware Compression Framework for HDF5-Based Synchrotron Workflows
entry.summary: PhotonZip: Lifecycle-Aware Compression for HDF5-Based Synchrotron Workflows arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Synchrotron detectors produce data at rates that strain storage and I/O systems. This paper presents PhotonZip, a compression framework that tests candidate modes through a common HDF5 path and selects measured configurations by compression ratio or round-trip throughput. Across four beamline-derived datasets, it reaches lossless compression ratios up to 1.629× and HDF5 write and read throughput up to 3.40 GB/s and 7.75 GB/s. Lossy preview modes provide up to 16× data reduction.

entry.title: Timely Status Delivery to a Ground Station Using UAV-Assisted Collection and Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: Timely Ground-Station Status Delivery via UAV-Assisted Data Collection and Hierarchical RL arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies a drone-assisted system in which a rotary-wing UAV gathers updates from multiple sensors, buffers them, and forwards selected updates to a ground station. It minimizes a weighted sum of ground-station age of information and UAV energy use, using a hierarchical actor-critic controller called HAE-AC. In a 100-sensor setup, the method reduces average ground-station age of information by about 22% compared with an adaptive staleness-gated benchmark.

entry.title: Survival-time risk in bursty packet loss: when simple channel models underestimate failure
entry.summary: Survival-Time Risk Beyond Low-Order Channel Models: Identifiability and Scheduling arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether low-order packet-loss statistics are enough to assess the risk that no update succeeds for a set number of consecutive slots under bursty losses. The authors analyze one-order-higher Markov channels that share these statistics under acknowledgment-based scheduling with transmission budgets. They find that low-order models can substantially underestimate the risk, so scheduling-dependent channel statistics are needed.

entry.title: Data-driven spectrum access technologies that let 6G share crowded radio bands.
entry.summary: Data-Driven Spectrum Access Technologies for 6G arXiv · Nov 3, 2026As mobile traffic grows, 6G needs new spectrum, but most bands below 15 GHz are already allocated to other services. The paper presents four data-driven techniques: coexistence protection for fixed incumbent receivers, control of radiated power above the horizon to protect satellite receivers, spectrum-sensing-based fast resource block blanking, and base-station-based occupancy detection. The techniques use artificial intelligence and extreme MIMO to enable coexistence and sharing while maintaining cellular performance.

entry.title: A new class of optimal binary linear complementary pairs of codes
entry.summary: A new class of optimal binary linear complementary pairs of codes arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes a new construction of optimal binary linear complementary pairs (LCPs) with θ=4, based on Belov codes. It extends the authors' earlier work on θ=3. The results yield many new optimal binary LCPs with flexible parameters, including more such pairs with smaller minimum distances.

entry.title: New lower bounds on kissing numbers in 32–35 and 37–39 dimensions
entry.summary: New lower bounds for kissing numbers in dimensions 32-35 and 37-39 arXiv · Oct 22, 2026The paper improves lower bounds on kissing numbers in dimensions 32–35 and 37–39, raising them to 352320, 370240, 390980, 415308, 499816, 605322 and 768916. For all dimensions except 38, the constructions follow Edel, Rains and Sloane, adding new binary constant-weight codes to the middle layer, with each extra codeword adding 128 points. For dimension 38, the authors add 6855 antipodal pairs from the Leech lattice's second shell to Kravatskiy's configuration.

entry.title: Deterministic causal quantization using shared representatives with bounded error
entry.summary: Deterministic Causal Quantization with Bounded Error: Adaptive Reconstruction and Entropy bounds arXiv · Oct 20, 2026The paper studies deterministic causal quantization that keeps pathwise error at most ε, where shared representatives are updated using only transmitted addresses. It compares address entropy rates with the process ε-entropy and bounds the gap for stationary sources with finite scalar ε-entropy. The authors also present results for uniform lattice grids, autoregressive Laplace and Gaussian sources, and stationary processes on finitely many centers.

entry.title: The Information Bottleneck Problem Is NP-hard
entry.summary: The Information Bottleneck and the Privacy Funnel are NP-hard arXiv · Oct 16, 2026This paper studies the information bottleneck method, which seeks a compressed representation of X that retains as much information as possible about Y, given a joint distribution on finite alphabets. The authors prove that computing the optimal value of this problem, including its Lagrangian relaxation, is NP-hard. Unless P equals NP, neither can be approximated in polynomial time within an additive error on the order of |X| to the power of negative 3/2. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that computing the information bottleneck and its Lagrangian relaxation is NP-hard, and that, unless P=NP, neither can be approximated in polynomial time within additive error of or

entry.title: Square-root-length MDS codes from hyperelliptic curves
entry.summary: MDS Algebraic Geometry Codes of Square-Root Length on Hyperelliptic Curves arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper constructs maximum distance separable (MDS) algebraic geometry codes over F_q for fixed genus g≥2 and any rate 0<ρ<1, for all sufficiently large odd squares q. The code length is about √q+1 plus O_g(q^{1/4}), with parameters [n,⌊ρn⌋,n-⌊ρn⌋+1]_q. The codes use full Riemann–Roch spaces on genus-g hyperelliptic curves. For large q they are not monomially equivalent to generalized Reed–Solomon (GRS) codes. ★★★★ Notable: For fixed genus g≥2 and 0<ρ<1, the authors construct MDS algebraic geometry codes of length about √q on hyperelliptic curves for large odd squares q, reporting they are not monomially equivalent to GR

entry.title: Information design for stable vehicle platooning
entry.summary: Information Design for Behaviorally Stable Platooning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies whether an informed operator can encourage voluntary vehicle platoon formation through a public disclosure rule. It builds a finite-vehicle coordination game and compares private joining costs with private observations of the corridor state, developing computational methods for persuasive disclosure. In a reference scenario, optimized two-message disclosure supports participation of 8.74% and 51.83%, versus zero without disclosure and 5.15% and 39.27% under full disclosure. The gains depend on favorable symmetric equilibrium selection.

entry.title: GPU engine for sparse matrix-vector products on compressed k²-tree graphs
entry.summary: A GPU Engine for Sparse Matrix-Vector Products on k²-Tree-Compressed Graphs arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a GPU engine that performs sparse matrix-vector multiplication directly on k²-trees, a compact representation of Boolean matrices. It descends the tree level by level, obtaining child positions from a parallel prefix sum or a sampled directory, and processes it in tiles so that temporary memory is bounded by the tree depth. Tested on NVIDIA GB10 and H100 with fourteen graphs of up to 1.2 billion edges, the tree is 2.3–27 times smaller than cuSPARSE's CSR, and a product on the largest graph needs 1.1 GB of device memory, 9 times less than cuSPARSE.

entry.title: Uniformly generating linear codes with a set hull size
entry.summary: Uniform Sampling of Linear Codes with Prescribed Hull Dimension arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents exactly uniform samplers for linear codes whose hull dimension is specified in advance, covering the Euclidean, Hermitian, and symplectic inner products over finite fields of every characteristic. Apart from the Euclidean case over fields of odd characteristic, these are the first uniform samplers for arbitrary prescribed hull dimension. Each sample requires an expected O(k²N + k log q) field operations.

entry.title: An information-geometric theory of distributed computation
entry.summary: An information-geometric formulation of distributed computation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces ΦID^IG, a geometric theory of information dynamics that captures irreducible collective computation in complex systems. It decomposes multi-input multi-output operations into interpretable computational modes, and validates the framework on discrete and Gaussian systems with known ground truth. The authors apply it to chaotic maps, the brain anatomy of over 100 mammalian species, and financial markets, reporting distinct computational profiles in each case.

entry.title: Beyond GNSS: Using LEO satellite signals for positioning via Doppler shifts
entry.summary: Beyond GNSS: Leveraging LEO Satellite Signals of Opportunity for Doppler Positioning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Low Earth orbit satellites move rapidly, causing significant Doppler shifts that can be used to locate user terminals, especially where GNSS is unavailable. The paper reviews the principles, challenges, and enabling technologies of signals-of-opportunity Doppler positioning. It also proposes SionnaNTN-RT, a ray tracing framework built on Sionna for simulating non-terrestrial networks. Simulations show high positioning accuracy in both urban and open-sky settings.

entry.title: ExaTract: scaling global brain tractography to large cohorts and ultra-high-resolution scans
entry.summary: Scaling global tractography with ExaTract: from large cohorts to ultra-high-resolution datasets arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents ExaTract, a parallel spin-glass tractography framework built for high-performance computing, implemented as an open-source MPI+Kokkos application. It splits the tractography domain into spatially overlapping regions processed across distributed memory nodes, with periodic synchronization of boundary changes to keep global convergence. The method is tested on in vivo and ex vivo diffusion MRI data, showing population-scale throughput on the full HCP dataset and producing the first mesoscopic structural connectome from global tractography on the high-resolution Chenonceau dataset.

entry.title: On inverse aggregate network assignment games: estimating how transport operators and travelers behave on a shared network from observed data.
entry.summary: On inverse aggregate network assignment games arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper extends aggregate assignment games to shared transport networks, offering path-based and link-based formulations with solution algorithms. It proposes an inverse optimization estimator for the link-based model, extended to capacitated two-sided markets. Calibrated on a Long Island Rail Road network of 897 nodes and 8,320 directed links, the method fits observed link flows well even when only 10-50% of links are sampled.

entry.title: At What Cost? Inefficiency in First-Price Procurement Auctions
entry.summary: At What Cost? (In)efficiency in First-Price Procurement Auctions arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies the efficiency of Bayes-Nash equilibria in first-price procurement auctions, measured by the Price of Anarchy, which compares equilibrium expected social cost to the optimal minimum. It shows that the standard format has no bounded efficiency guarantee. It then introduces a phantom bidder mechanism to restore a finite bound. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show unbounded PoA for standard first-price procurement, derive a tight bound, and propose phantom-bidder mechanisms with matching lower bounds.

entry.title: Non-coherent over-the-air distributed consensus: algorithm design and power control optimization
entry.summary: Non-Coherent Over-the-Air Distributed Consensus: Algorithm Design and Power Control Optimization arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a non-coherent over-the-air (NCOTA) consensus framework for distributed average consensus in wireless networks, requiring neither instantaneous channel state information nor phase alignment. It proposes a decentralized projected gradient descent algorithm with row-stochastic mixing (DPGD-RS) and proves its mean-square convergence to the exact average of the agents' initial states. The authors also derive a closed-form bound on the mean-square consensus error and a spectral-reshaping power control scheme that jointly optimizes transmit powers and receive-scaling factors, which converges faster than full-power transmission and spectral-radius-minimization benchmarks in numerical results.

entry.title: Classifying good rational functions of degree up to six
entry.summary: Good rational functions up to degree six arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies locally recoverable codes, which underpin modern distributed storage systems. It completes the classification of good rational functions of degree up to 6 in characteristic 2, using algebraic function field theory to determine their minimal arithmetic and geometric Galois groups. The authors prove that the exact number of totally split places over extension fields follows a linear recurring sequence. This provides an efficient way to compute the exact lengths and dimensions of the corresponding optimal LRCs.

entry.title: uTECH Turbo-MOVES: Faster Vehicle Emissions Modeling Through Software Architecture
entry.summary: uTECH Turbo-MOVES: The Intersection of Software Architectural Innovation and Sustainable Mobility Analysis arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents uTECH Turbo-MOVES, a software architecture that speeds up computation in the U.S. EPA's Motor Vehicle Emission Simulator (MOVES) without changing its Calculator modules or input/output structure. It combines RunSpec partitioning, container isolation, in-memory intermediate storage, and concurrent workload orchestration. Across six benchmark cases, it reports a measured 5.5x and an estimated 15.3x per-run speedup for Default-scale workloads, and an 84.8x campaign speedup for an eight-county Emission Rates analysis.

entry.title: Pricing LLM services from a cold start under two-sided learning
entry.summary: Cold-Start Pricing of LLM Services under Two-Sided Learning arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies how providers of online large language model services can set prices when they lack historical data, while users' willingness to pay changes with repeated use. It models the problem as two-sided learning, where the user learns from private experience and the provider adjusts prices using only purchase decisions. The authors derive matching minimax regret bounds across two serving-cost regimes and propose corresponding algorithms. Simulations confirm the predicted regret scaling and show the algorithms outperform standard online learning baselines. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formulate LLM pricing cold start as two-sided learning, derive matching minimax regret bounds with a cost-dependent phase transition, and report simulations supporting the predicted scalin

entry.title: Using Antenna Mutual Coupling to Boost Cell-Free Massive MIMO
entry.summary: Harnessing Mutual Coupling in Cell-Free mMIMO arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies a cell-free massive MIMO system in which several access points each use a small, fixed-size linear antenna array with possibly closely spaced antennas. Using multiport communication theory, the authors analyze how mutual coupling affects uplink and downlink spectral efficiency under different impedance-matching strategies. Numerical results show that with a full matching network, mutual coupling can itself be beneficial when an access point serves several user devices.

entry.title: Allocating Verification in LLM Agent Pipelines with Hidden Tool Degradation: A Mean-Field Analysis
entry.summary: Verification Allocation in Stylized LLM Agent Pipelines under Hidden Tool Degradation: A Discrete-Time Mean-Field Analysis arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper studies a simplified model of verification allocation in role-structured LLM agent pipelines where errors are inherited and tools may degrade silently. It establishes fixed-point results for serial and multi-role pipelines and a finite-population deviation bound under independence. Under explicit conditions it characterizes a two-action threshold policy and a restricted four-action interval policy, which synthetic experiments are used to check. The analysis is conditional on the model and is not a general mean-field-game result or empirical evidence about deployed LLM systems.

entry.title: Covering radius of the third-order Reed–Muller code RM(3,8) is 56
entry.summary: The Covering Radius of the Reed--Muller Code texorpdfstringRM(3,8)RM(3,8) is 56 arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper proves that the covering radius of the third-order Reed–Muller code in eight variables is 56. The proof splits even- and odd-weight inputs, using moment-controlled slicing and a covariance-rank obstruction. Explicitly stated local covering and compatibility assertions are verified by complete finite certificates.

entry.title: Multi-GPU acceleration of interface problems in FEniCS for cardiac modeling.
entry.summary: Multi-GPU Acceleration of Interface Problems in FEniCS, with Application to Cardiac Modeling arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper extends cuDOLFINx so that mixed-dimensional interface problems can be assembled on GPUs within the FEniCS framework. Combined with GPU-resident Krylov solvers and algebraic multigrid preconditioning, it runs the EMI cardiac model end to end on GPUs. Strong and weak scaling experiments on regular and realistic 3D cardiac geometries, with up to 8000 cells and 22 million degrees of freedom, compare GPU and CPU performance.

entry.title: Searching a plane using lines between robot pairs: competitive ratios for two and many robots
entry.summary: Searching the Plane in the Segment Visibility Model arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies deterministic search by several unit-speed robots starting at the origin of the plane, where a target is found once it lies on a segment joining two robots. For two robots, the optimal competitive ratio is 1+√3+π/6 when the target distance is known, and lies between about 3.286 and 8.929 when it is unknown. For three or more robots, the competitive ratio is sec(π/n) whether or not the distance is known.

entry.title: Reed-Muller codes are optimal linear 3-query locally correctable codes
entry.summary: Reed-Muller Codes are Optimal Binary Linear 3-Query LCCs arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proves that any linear 3-query locally correctable code with constant correction radius must have length at least 2 raised to Ω(√k). The previous best lower bound was 2 raised to Ω(√(k/log k)). The result shows that linear 3-LCCs built from Reed-Muller codes, which have length 2 raised to O(√k), are optimal up to constant factors in the exponent. The proof combines chain-derived equations with Kikuchi graphs and shows that a certain edge-coloured Kikuchi graph has a unique colour cycle. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the length lower bound for linear 3-query LCCs to 2^Ω(√k), showing Reed-Muller constructions are optimal up to constant exponent factors.

entry.title: Dynamic coalition formation under capacity limits: a regime-switching value-investing game
entry.summary: Dynamic Coalition Formation Under Capacity Constraints: A Regime-Switching Value-Investing Game arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies how a network operator and service providers coordinate investment and resource allocation for edge computing under uncertain demand. It proposes an audit-based framework for daily coalition formation, using a two-stage coalitional game that separates infrastructure investment from operational participation, with demand modeled as a geometric random walk. In a reference run over five service classes and three years, the approach gains 12.4% over static grand-coalition membership and recovers 94.6% of the full-information optimum.

entry.title: Deep reinforcement learning for multi-drone communication aided by BD-RIS and RSMA
entry.summary: Deep Reinforcement Learning for BD-RIS-Assisted Multi-UAV RSMA Communications arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies a downlink in which multiple drones communicate through a hybrid setup using beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (BD-RIS) and rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA). Drones in good BD-RIS coverage use both direct and reflected links, while others use direct links only. The authors jointly optimize drone trajectories, RSMA rate allocation, beamforming, BD-RIS matrices and drone-to-surface association using a DDPG-based method. Simulations show a sum rate comparable to SAC and higher than TD3, PPO and DQN, at about 1/65 of the per-slot runtime of fixed-trajectory alternating optimization, with gains coming mainly from RSMA.

entry.title: Hotplug Coded Caching: Uncoded vs. Row-Wise Coded Placement Comparison
entry.summary: Hotplug Coded Caching: Uncoded versus Row-Wise Coded Placements arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies the hotplug coded caching model, where K users fill caches of size M from N files, but only an unknown set of A users is active during delivery. Under uncoded placement, it shows that YMA delivery with MAN placement is optimal, and offline users incur a load penalty at intermediate memory sizes. Under row-wise placement, classical schemes are embedded in Reed-Solomon codes, yielding the classical tradeoff for A users with no load penalty, though the placement depends on K. The paper also derives converse bounds showing several of these schemes are optimal under specific conditions.

entry.title: A game-theory method for settling real-time energy imbalances in local communities
entry.summary: A Cooperative Game-Theoretic Framework for Real-Time Deviation Settlement in Local Energy Communities arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes a cooperative game-theoretic framework for settling real-time deviations in community-based local energy markets. The settlement process is modeled as a transferable-utility cooperative game, and the Shapley value and nucleolus are compared with a proportional imbalance responsibility rule. The framework is demonstrated using real-world data from a residential energy community in Amsterdam.

entry.title: DisC: Game-Based Incentive Design for Fair, Robust, Energy-Efficient Client Participation in Over-the-Air Federated Learning
entry.summary: DisC: Incentive Design for Green, Robust, and Fair Client Self-Participation in OTA Federated Learning arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper addresses over-the-air federated learning (OTA-FL), where client heterogeneity, fading channels, energy limits, and uneven participation can harm fairness and aggregation accuracy. It proposes DisC, a game-theoretic distributed client selection framework in which each client chooses its participation level by maximizing a utility that accounts for fairness, learning relevance, OTA distortion, energy use, and delay. The authors show that DisC has a Nash equilibrium and can be formulated as an exact potential game.

entry.title: GPU-parallel AC N-1 contingency analysis using low-rank updates to a shared Jacobian
entry.summary: Low-rank corrections to a shared reference Jacobian for GPU-parallel AC N\!-\!1 contingency analysis arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents a GPU-parallel Newton–Raphson solver for N-1 contingency analysis, which checks power system performance after single-element outages. It inverts one reference Jacobian matrix and reuses it across all contingencies, handling topology changes with low-rank Woodbury corrections and remaining state perturbations with an inner iterative solver. On transmission-scale benchmarks, per-topology solve times are competitive with an optimized 80-core CPU baseline, with the low-rank correction accounting for about 1–2% of the workload.

entry.title: Joint Port Position and Beamforming Optimization for Fluid Antenna Near-Field Sensing
entry.summary: Fluid Antenna Array-Enabled Near-Field ISAC: Joint Port Position Optimization and Transmit Beamforming Design arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes a planar fluid antenna array-assisted near-field integrated sensing and communication framework for multiuser communication and target sensing. The authors derive the Fisher information matrix and Cramér-Rao bound for jointly estimating target range, zenith angle, azimuth angle, and radial velocity. They jointly optimize the array port positions and transmit beamforming under communication SINR, transmit power, and deployment constraints, using a two-stage alternating algorithm. Simulations indicate favorable sensing performance with reasonable computational cost.

entry.title: Same function, different CPU: how hardware differences affect serverless cost and speed
entry.summary: Same Function, Different CPU: Quantifying Hardware Heterogeneity in Commercial FaaS Platforms arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies how the type of CPU a function runs on affects its performance across four commercial Function-as-a-Service platforms. Using variance decomposition, it finds CPU heterogeneity alone explains 4% to 97% of performance variance on AWS Lambda and Google Cloud Run Functions, while Azure Functions shows a platform mechanism that overshadows CPU effects. Because all platforms bill by duration, invocations on the slowest CPU type can cost up to three times as much as those on the fastest.

entry.title: Cluster Efficiency for LLM Serving via Fast Interconnects
entry.summary: Introducing Cluster Efficiency to LLM Serving: Pooling Economical Accelerators over Fast Interconnects arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies cluster efficiency for long-context LLM serving, measured in tokens per dollar and per joule, using economical accelerators pooled over fast interconnects. The authors implement their serving stack on a Tenstorrent Galaxy cluster of Blackhole chips, combining integrated communication engines, pipelined ring transfers, communication-computation overlap, and device-side decode replay. Across three dense models in BF16 and 8-bit configurations with 8K to 256K-token contexts, the Galaxy achieves 1.07 to 2.24 times the tokens per dollar of an eight-GPU RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell server. Emulating TCP-class communication reduces throughput by 23.5% to 67.4% and removes the cost advantage in every evaluated configuration.

entry.title: Dispatch control for multi-tenant workflows under multi-resource external rate limits
entry.summary: Dispatch Control for Priority-Based, Multi-Tenant Workflows under Multi-Resource External Rate Limits arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper addresses workflow engines calling external APIs with shared rate limits, where retried throttled calls hold worker slots and starve other tenants. The authors propose Backpressure, a worker-side admission gate that atomically checks each call's cost against shared state, enforces fairness over both requests and tokens, and releases worker slots for denied calls to wait on durable timers. On a three-priority workload, it raises Jain's fairness index from 0.60 to 0.89 and cuts high-priority tail latency roughly eightfold.

entry.title: Customizing wireless channels with reflecting surfaces: feasibility and limits
entry.summary: Customizing Wireless Channels via Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces: Feasibility, Fundamental Limits, and Constructive Design arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies whether a phase-only intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) can reshape the wireless channel between a base station and a user into a prescribed form, under three progressively relaxed criteria. It draws on a mathematical link to the signal error of a point-to-point MIMO system to characterize per-coordinate gain limits and derives array-size conditions for avoiding phase conflicts among streams. Numerical results show that jointly choosing singular vectors and IRS phase shifts reduces average customization error, but gains beyond the propagation spectral limits cannot be achieved exactly.

entry.title: Persuasion by Parts: Separate Sources Persuade Through Independent Coordinates
entry.summary: Persuasion by Parts arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper studies how an information designer can persuade a receiver to act when the payoff depends on independent coordinates observed by separate sources. The designer commits to a product experiment in which each source conditions its signal only on its own coordinate. When the receiver's decision rule is known, the achievable probability of action is at least a constant times the square of the joint-persuasion probability, and the exponent 2 is tight. When the rule is unknown, a product experiment built from the prior alone achieves an exponent of 2 plus epsilon.

entry.title: Predicting GPU latency on low-end devices without collecting traces from them
entry.summary: Local Zero-Shot Latency Prediction for Low-End GPUs arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes a zero-shot method for predicting execution latency on low-end consumer GPUs without collecting execution traces on each target device. It configures a local host GPU by selectively modifying device parameters so that its measured latencies approximate those of the target hardware. Evaluated on 60 computer-vision models across 21 consumer GPU models, the method reaches a mean absolute percentage error of 14.21%, versus more than 25% for comparable baselines. Predicted and measured latencies show an average Spearman correlation of 0.961.

entry.title: Analyzing Position Estimation Error in Cooperative OFDM Sensing-and-Communication Systems
entry.summary: Localization MSE Analysis for Cooperative OFDM-ISAC arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper develops a receiver-specific mean-squared-error framework for localization in cooperative integrated sensing and communication systems that use random OFDM payloads. It analyzes local peak perturbations and incorrect ambiguity-peak selection for matched filtering and reciprocal filtering. Matched filtering is examined for how symbol-energy fluctuations cause frequency spread and interference that affect delay errors, while reciprocal filtering removes symbol-dependent weighting but amplifies noise for low-energy symbols. Numerical results show receiver-dependent estimation errors and the benefits of frequency-dependent constellation allocation.

entry.title: Graph Conditions for Angle Rigidity and Angle-Based Network Localization
entry.summary: Equivalent Graphical Conditions for Angle Rigidity and Angle-Based Network Localization arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies angle rigidity, a theory that characterizes the geometric shape of planar graphs under angle constraints and supports global convergence of angle-based network localization algorithms. It establishes the equivalence between angle constraints and bearing constraints and gives conditions under which cycle compatible frameworks are angle fixable. The authors show for the first time that Laman graphs characterize minimally globally angle rigid graphs. They also propose a distributed algorithm for angle-based sensor network localization that guarantees global convergence under a milder topology condition than prior work.

entry.title: Rose: Graph Optimization and GPU Resource Control for Efficient Embodied RL
entry.summary: Rose: Efficient Embodied RL through Graph Optimization and GPU Compute Resource Control arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents Rose, a runtime-aware system that automates fine-grained overlap and GPU resource management for embodied reinforcement learning while preserving synchronous training semantics. It first uses a window-guided graph optimizer to find low-activity GPU windows and overlap complementary work, then uses NVIDIA MPS with a slack-aware resource manager to tune per-process SM quotas. Across diverse policies, simulators, RL algorithms, and GPU platforms, Rose reportedly achieves 1.20 to 1.92 times higher training throughput and 23.8% to 39.3% higher average SM activity than state-of-the-art systems.

entry.title: X-PASS: Pinching-antenna systems using radially arranged waveguides, designed and analyzed
entry.summary: Design and Analysis of Pinching-Antenna Systems With Radially Deployed Waveguides (X-PASS) arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes X-PASS, in which a central hub feeds several radially arranged waveguide arms, each carrying one pinching antenna, and operates them by selecting, aggregating, or multiplexing the arms. The authors model the hub's insertion losses and derive a unified signal-to-noise ratio expression for the three operating modes. They also give a closed-form radius inside which aggregation outperforms selection. Numerical results validate the analysis and compare X-PASS coverage with other layouts at equal transmit power.

entry.title: Information cost of inner product and matrix multiplication, via a Shannon-to-min-entropy conversion
entry.summary: Information Complexity of Inner Product and Matrix Multiplication via Shannon-to-Min-Entropy Conversion arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper determines the information complexity of matrix multiplication over finite fields with independent uniform inputs, up to a universal additive constant. For the binary inner product, it resolves an open question posed by Braverman, Garg, Pankratov, and Weinstein about the optimal dependence on error probability. The proof relies on a new theorem about convolution on discrete groups, stating that with enough distributions, the min-entropy of their ordered product is at least the average Shannon entropy minus a constant.

entry.title: OctEx: GPU vector search over billions of vectors using precomputed lattice neighbor lists
entry.summary: OctEx: Billion-Scale Vector Search by Precomputed Lattice Neighbor Lists on GPUs arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents OctEx, a GPU system for approximate nearest-neighbor vector search that stores hundreds of randomly projected dataset copies in GPU memory. Each copy assigns vectors to nearly round cells of a regular grid and precomputes the nearest vectors to each cell center, so queries read candidates in parallel rather than through many dependent graph-walk rounds. On four H100 GPUs at recall 0.95 to 0.995, the authors report speedups of 2.0x to 46.4x over CAGRA on datasets up to one hundred million vectors, and 1.46x to 2.05x on one-billion-vector datasets.

entry.title: When cache pressure becomes a trap: metastable failures in LLM agent serving
entry.summary: When Cache Pressure Becomes a Trap: Metastability in Agent Serving arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper studies how a brief traffic surge can break prefix reuse for LLM agents in prefill-decode disaggregated serving engines, leaving service degraded even after load returns to previously sustainable levels. The authors attribute this to a population-cache feedback loop explained by a fluid model. They present Basin, a scheduling approach that reserves predicted session contexts, extends cache with idle decode memory, and sheds excess demand, reporting higher goodput than Continuum and HiCache on real H200 deployments. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors identify cache-population feedback as a metastable failure mechanism in PD-disaggregated serving, propose a fluid model and the Basin policy, and report goodput gains on real H200 deployme

entry.title: Time-Aware Urban Flood Routing Using Forecast Water Depth and Sticky Road Closures
entry.summary: Time-Aware Urban Flood Routing with Sticky Edge Closure on Forecast Depth: A Hanoi Case Study arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents a routing engine that uses a two-hour water forecast, updated every 15 minutes, to plan trips around roads closed for a given vehicle class. Any road closing mid-trip stays closed for that query. In tests on a recorded storm in western Hanoi, a router checking only departure conditions sent 7.8% of routes onto roads flooded by arrival. The water depths come from an unverified hydrodynamic simulation, and the rainfall was replayed rather than forecast live.

entry.title: Finding the best measurement sequence when a measuring device is broken or limited
entry.summary: Finding optimal measurement sequences for broken or constrained measuring devices arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper addresses how to choose the best sequence of measurements from the remaining available ones when a measuring device is worn, damaged, or malfunctioning. It frames this as a sequential decision process using information theory and dynamic programming. The authors show that greedy measurement sequences are suboptimal for a simple class of constraints, and propose an algorithm related to optimal binary decision trees with derived complexity bounds.

entry.title: Designing finite-state channels in reverse using dynamic measure matching
entry.summary: Inverse Design of Finite-State Channels by Dynamic Measure Matching arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies an inverse problem for communication channels with memory: constructing a finite-state channel for which a given signaling behavior supports capacity-achieving codes. It introduces dynamic measure matching to turn a directed-information converse into conditions on channel dynamics, defining a notion of dynamic surprise. For a specific noisy refractory family, the paper establishes an exact capacity plateau, differences between Shannon and zero-error feedback capacities, and an exponential strong converse.

entry.title: A sharp upper bound on mutual information between two binary variables
entry.summary: A Sharp Mutual Information Bound for Binary Pairs arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper proves a sharp upper bound on the mutual information between two binary random variables, expressed through their distribution-dependent KL contraction coefficient. It resolves the binary-pair conjecture of Anantharam, Gohari, Kamath, and Nair. Equality holds exactly when the variables are independent or form a doubly symmetric binary source. Combined with tensorization and data processing, the result also bounds mutual information between binary outputs from two correlated observation sequences, and this bound depends only on one pair's law when observation pairs are independent copies. ★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve the binary-pair conjecture, giving a tight bound on mutual information via the KL contraction coefficient and characterizing equality cases with supporting-tangent arguments.

entry.title: A beam-switched sparse circular array that reduces angle-estimation errors in Wi-Fi sensing.
entry.summary: A Beam-Switched Sparse Circular Array for Passive Wi-Fi Sensing arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper addresses the need for unambiguous angle-of-arrival estimation across the full azimuth plane in Wi-Fi sensing. It proposes an angularly staggered beam-switched uniform circular array that uses spatial complementarity to suppress grating-lobe ambiguities without adding RF chains. Numerical evaluations show significantly fewer AoA estimation outliers and better omnidirectional tracking performance.

entry.title: Coalitions and Stability Frameworks Unifying Majoritarian and Proportional Multiwinner Allocation
