entry.title: Sensor-side hardwired units for parallel vision pre-processing that frees the host CPU
entry.summary: Hardwired Distributed Processing Units at the Sensor: Truly Parallel Vision Pre-Processing that Frees the Host CPU arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper proposes placing small, fixed hardware datapaths (HDPUs) directly at the image sensor, each performing one always-on task in parallel on the pixel stream and sending only compact results to the host. The authors build three units (Canny edges, Harris corners, and a line tracker that issues steering decisions) on a low-cost Artix-7 FPGA using 2,568 LUTs and an estimated 0.318 W. A full-system simulation compares these units with a frame-based host program, showing much earlier responses and lower host CPU load. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose sensor-attached hardwired units for parallel vision pre-processing, implement them on an Artix-7 FPGA, and report full-system simulation comparisons against host latency.

entry.title: Upper bounds on CSP non-redundancy using locally decodable codes
entry.summary: Upper Bounds for CSP Non-redundancy via Locally Decodable Codes arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies non-redundancy in constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs), which measures how many logically independent clauses a CSP instance can contain. The authors present a new method that uses locally decodable codes (LDCs) and locally correctable codes (LCCs) to upper-bound the non-redundancy of certain relations. Applying this approach, they obtain improved upper bounds for the BCK predicate and its Boolean variant, and give the first Boolean predicate whose non-redundancy provably is not of the form n^{k±o(1)}. ★★★★ Notable: The authors bound CSP non-redundancy via 2-query LDC and LCC structure, improving BCK bounds and reporting a first Boolean predicate outside the n^{k±o(1)} form.

entry.title: SCL-Aware Design of PAC Codes: Designing Error-Correcting Codes for List Decoding
entry.summary: An SCL-Aware Design of PAC Codes arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents design methods for the rate profile of polarization-adjusted convolutional (PAC) codes intended for successive cancellation list (SCL) decoding. It introduces a conditional density evolution Gaussian approximation (CDEGA) to analyze decoding with errors, and a dangerous-path occupancy metric to measure bit-error occupancy in a finite list. Using these tools, the authors design codes of length up to 512 that reportedly achieve at least half a dB gain over traditional PAC codes at an FER of 10^-3.

entry.title: SPECTRUM: A Blueprint and Strategy for Europe's Exascale Research Data and Compute Infrastructure
entry.summary: SPECTRUM: A Strategic Framework and Technical Blueprint for European Exascale Research Data and Compute Infrastructure arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper summarises two SPECTRUM project documents: a Technical Blueprint and a Strategic Research, Innovation and Deployment Agenda (SRIDA). It notes that the HiLumi LHC, SKA Observatory and LOFAR 2.0 will push high energy physics and radio astronomy towards exabyte-scale data within a decade. The documents share the same evidence base, offering technical recommendations and a phased roadmap of priorities. The paper also describes their consultative method and the impact the SRIDA expects.

entry.title: Can Language Models Be Trusted to Orchestrate Edge-Cloud Services?
entry.summary: Can We Rely on Language Models to Orchestrate Services across the Edge-Cloud Continuum? arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper systematically reviews 39 primary studies on using language models to orchestrate services across the edge-cloud continuum. It proposes a five-dimensional framework linking system context, orchestration decisions, language model agency, operational safeguards, and evaluation evidence. The review finds mostly hybrid designs, where language models support interpretation, candidate generation, and mitigation planning, while downstream components typically keep feasibility enforcement and execution authority.

entry.title: First-order bilevel optimization for designing non-truthful auctions
entry.summary: First-Order Bilevel Optimization for Non-truthful Auction Design arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper formulates auction design as a Stackelberg game with multiple strategic followers and proposes a fully first-order algorithm for revenue optimization in non-truthful auctions. It establishes non-asymptotic guarantees for hypergradient approximation and shows that, under standard smoothness and strong-monotonicity assumptions, the method reaches an O(ε)-stationary point with about Õ(ε⁻²) first-order oracle calls. Experiments on single-item and multi-item auctions report faster convergence than second- and zeroth-order baselines, better scaling with more bidders, and auctions whose revenue approaches that of truthful baselines.

entry.title: True 3D Holography: Future Communication Service and Requirements for Converged Cloud-Network Architecture toward 6G
entry.summary: True 3D Holography: A Communication Service of Tomorrow and Its Requirements for a New Converged Cloud and Network Architecture on the Path to 6G arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines true 3D holographic communication as a use case in the 6G NeXt research project and sets out its requirements for communication and computing infrastructure. It argues that such services need high processing power, a high-speed distributed backbone supporting split computing, and tight integration between processing facilities and wireless networks. The authors propose an overall communication and computing architecture and discuss novel technological approaches based on it.

entry.title: Measuring How Much Communication Helps Multi-Agent Target Tracking at Limited Data Rates
entry.summary: Measuring the Value of Communication in Multi-Agent Tracking Under Finite-Rate Belief Sharing arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies how useful communication is for stationary agents cooperatively tracking a moving target when they can only exchange information at limited rates. Each agent uses range and bearing measurements with an extended Kalman filter, quantizes its state estimate, and fuses shared information via covariance intersection. Results show very low rates can hurt performance due to coarse quantization, while moderate rates capture most of the gain, with diminishing returns at higher rates.

entry.title: PhOSv1: Scaling model sleeping on one server by sharing GPU contexts for faster autoscaling
entry.summary: PhOSv1: Efficient Scaling of Model Sleeping on a Single Server for Autoscaling with GPU-Context Deduplication arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper addresses autoscaling in model-as-a-service systems, where existing model sleeping methods keep each sleeping model's GPU context resident, so the cost grows with the number of models. The authors present PhOSv1, which routes each engine's GPU context allocation through a central daemon via API remoting, deduplicating shared contexts. This lets a single server keep many more models asleep. The evaluation reports scale-up time matching vanilla vLLM sleep mode while substantially reducing GPU memory footprint.

entry.title: An exact parallel dense Gauss-Seidel method trading parallel runtime for preprocessing time
entry.summary: An Exact Parallel Dense Gauss-Seidel Algorithm with Trade-Offs between Parallel Execution Time and Preprocessing Time arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The Gauss-Seidel method is widely used for solving linear equation systems because it converges well, but its data dependencies make parallelization difficult. This paper proposes a new parallel Gauss-Seidel algorithm that achieves better parallel runtimes in exchange for more preprocessing time. The algorithm can be tuned to offer trade-offs between preprocessing time and the best achievable parallel runtime.

entry.title: TRACEs: An Embedded Provenance Architecture for Distributed Scientific Workflows
entry.summary: TRACEs: Fine-Grained Embedded Provenance for Distributed Scientific Workflows arXiv · Oct 29, 2026Large-scale scientific workflows run on distributed HPC resources, which makes it hard to explain how data products are generated and why similar runs give different results. TRACEs is a provenance architecture for distributed containerized workflows that embeds data lineage and execution context directly in every generated data artifact, and it stays compatible with existing workflow management systems. Evaluated on a seven-stage E. coli variant-calling workflow across multiple HPC nodes, it achieved 100% provenance completeness under distributed execution. It also traced a 200-fold difference in variant counts to differences in input sequencing data without re-executing the workflow.

entry.title: Level crossing rate bounds for products of independent nonstationary fading processes
entry.summary: Level Crossing Rate Bounds for Products of Independent Nonstationary Fading Processes arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper develops a unified framework for the instantaneous total level crossing rate (LCR) of products of independent positive nonstationary fading processes. Universal upper and lower bounds are derived from an exact decomposition of the product derivative and signed crossing imbalance, using only factor-wise crossing statistics. The authors introduce a drifting Gaussian-derivative (DGD) class, giving bounds via an exact Gaussian-mixture representation that capture aggregate drift and derivative fluctuations. Numerical results show that the DGD bounds closely bracket the exact LCR.

entry.title: Optimal self-orthogonal binary linear codes
entry.summary: Optimal self-orthogonal binary linear codes arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper completes the determination of the minimum possible length of eight-dimensional binary self-orthogonal codes with a given minimum distance. For nine-dimensional codes it gives exact values and bounds for minimum distance up to 64. Using a geometric view of linear codes as multisets of points, the authors redo the classification for dimensions up to seven without computer assistance. They also prove that [93,9,44]_2 codes do not exist.

entry.title: Information geometry of Sinkhorn divergence on a Hilbert manifold
entry.summary: The information geometry of the Sinkhorn divergence on a Hilbert manifold arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies the metric tensor that the Sinkhorn divergence, a debiased entropic optimal transport cost, induces on probability measures defined along curves. The authors construct a real-analytic Hilbert manifold on which this tensor is a weak Riemannian metric, and extend Eguchi's geometric construction to third order. They also show the metric is bounded above by a multiple of the Fisher-Rao metric on the smooth stratum.

entry.title: Dynamic Resource Scaling for Quantum Circuit Simulations on HPC Systems
entry.summary: Enabling Dynamic Resource Scaling in Quantum Circuit Simulations arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper makes the QuEST state-vector simulator malleable using the DMR framework, so one job can resize its node allocation between quantum circuits with different qubit counts. Because no state vector persists between circuits, resizing needs no data redistribution, and a checkpoint of the next circuit's index allows resumption. The authors evaluate reconfiguration overhead on MareNostrum 5 and show that a single job can run circuits of varying sizes with negligible overhead.

entry.title: Support-distribution conditions for MSRD codes reduce to one inequality
entry.summary: The Support-Distribution Conditions for MSRD Codes Reduce to a Single Inequality arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies linear maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD) codes and counts codewords with a prescribed nonzero support. It proves that a family of nonnegativity conditions, conjectured by Byrne, Gluesing-Luerssen, and Ravagnani, is equivalent to a single condition at the vector of total dimension d+1 obtained by filling the longest blocks first. The result yields an explicit existence criterion over every finite field. The paper also shows an infinite family of parameters that satisfies the joint condition yet admits no such linear code.

entry.title: Energy-efficient uplink RSMA using a Rydberg atomic quantum receiver
entry.summary: Improving Energy Efficiency of Uplink RSMA via Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receiver arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies an uplink rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) network that uses a Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (RAQR) to maximize energy efficiency. To handle the direct-readout RAQR's amplitude-only measurements, the authors propose a phase alignment mechanism that linearizes the received signal while keeping channel energy. For symmetric rate requirements, they derive closed-form power allocation from KKT conditions, while for asymmetric requirements they propose a block coordinate descent power allocation and a low-complexity paired allocation scheme. Simulations show the KKT-based scheme achieves the highest energy efficiency, and the low-complexity scheme cuts computation with moderate efficiency loss.

entry.title: Length limits for MDS algebraic geometry codes from curves of any positive genus
entry.summary: Length Bounds for MDS Algebraic Geometry Codes of Arbitrary Positive Genus arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies the length of maximum distance separable (MDS) algebraic geometry codes built from curves of arbitrary positive genus. For fixed genus, it proves that the ratio of length to field size is asymptotically at most 1/2 when both dimension and codimension grow faster than the logarithm of the field size. It also gives explicit bounds under logarithmic dimension conditions. The bounds hold in every characteristic and do not depend on the choice of curve or evaluation set. The proof combines character sums on the Jacobian with an estimate for sums of distinct points.

entry.title: A uniform upper bound on the length of MDS codes from genus-two curves
entry.summary: A Uniform Upper Bound on the Length of MDS Codes from Genus-Two Curves arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies the maximal length of MDS algebraic geometry codes built from genus-two curves over finite fields. For codes of length n and dimension k with 3≤k≤n-3, the authors prove n<(2q+10√q+16)/3 for every prime power q, regardless of the parity of k. This gives a uniform upper bound of 2q/3+O(√q), which is strictly smaller than q+1 when q≥125.

entry.title: Secure wireless communication using flexible reflectors: joint optimization of their position and rotation for physical-layer security
entry.summary: Secure Wireless Communications with Flexible Reflectors: Joint Position and Rotation Optimization for Physical Layer Security arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies secure communication over non-line-of-sight links aided by flexible reflectors (FRs), passive metallic plates on movable platforms, and jointly optimizes their positions and rotations to maximize the secrecy rate. For a single FR, it proposes a Fibonacci segmentation search (FSS) method and a lower-complexity cross-entropy search (CES) method, then extends both to multiple FRs. Simulations show FSS achieves significant secrecy rate gains over benchmarks, while CES offers a favorable runtime-performance tradeoff.

entry.title: Speeding up finite Markov chains via Bregman projections and partition design
entry.summary: Bregman projections and partition design for accelerating finite Markov chains arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies Gibbs averaging of finite Markov chains with a prescribed stationary distribution, built from a Gibbs kernel induced by a state-space partition. It proves that the projected chain GPG is an information projection for admissible Bregman generators, with a Pythagorean identity and a dual characterization. For reversible ergodic baselines, Gibbs averaging does not increase the squared weighted Frobenius distance to stationarity, so the mixing time does not increase. The paper also gives partition-selection objectives and algorithms, and a numerical experiment compares the projected chains with a local Metropolis sampler.

entry.title: Fragmented Obedient Equilibria in Routing Games: a new equilibrium concept for competing mediators recommending routes
entry.summary: Fragmented Obedient Equilibria in Routing Games arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies routing games where competing mediators recommend routes to fixed nonatomic populations. Each mediator chooses a randomized flow allocation to minimize its population's expected travel cost, subject to users having no conditional expected gain above a tolerance ε from ignoring recommendations. The authors define fragmented obedient equilibria (FOE) and prove existence under a lower-hemicontinuity assumption on obedient policy correspondences. Under affine edge latencies, the problem reduces exactly to first and second flow moments, and for networks with at most four routes each best response is a semidefinite program. A Braess network example shows that relaxing obedience can lower FOE costs, though gaps to the social optimum and optimal obedient pooling can persist.

entry.title: PDScope: Resolving the Prefill-Decode Trade-off in Memory-Limited MoE Inference
entry.summary: PDScope: Breaking the Prefill-Decode Seesaw for Memory-Bound MoE Inference arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper addresses local deployment of MoE-based LLMs on CPU-GPU nodes, where limited GPU memory forces most experts into CPU memory. Prefill is compute-bound and favors aggressive GPU loading, while decode is I/O-bound and needs conservative transfers, creating a trade-off under low batching. PDScope decouples the two phases, predicting expert activations and optimizing placement, prefetching, and execution for each, using a static computation graph, cache prefetching, and zero-copy asynchronous I/O. On mainstream MoE models, it reports 2.5-10.3x higher prefill throughput and 2.1-6.1x higher decode throughput than existing systems.

entry.title: Phase retrieval of bandlimited signals via Morlet and companion wavelets
entry.summary: Phase Retrieval of Bandlimited Signals Using a Morlet Wavelet and an Admissible Companion arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper shows that complex bandlimited signals can be uniquely recovered, up to a global phase factor, from two families of wavelet transform magnitudes. These families arise from translations of a fixed dilated Morlet wavelet and a fixed companion wavelet, sampled at twice the Nyquist rate in two frequency bins. The authors reformulate both families as modulated Gaussian convolution measurements of an auxiliary bandlimited signal and apply a Gaussian convolution uniqueness result. They prove that samples on (4B)^{-1}Z determine every signal in PW_B^2, using significantly fewer sampling points than earlier wavelet phase retrieval methods.

entry.title: Consumer welfare limits of market segmentation when some consumers are captive
entry.summary: The Welfare Limits of Market Segmentation with Captive Consumers arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies a duopoly with captive and contested consumers and characterizes every pair of consumer and producer surplus achievable under some market composition and some public segmentation, constructing a market for each pair. The achievable set is lens-shaped. At any industry profit level, consumer welfare is lowest when captive and contested consumers are perfectly separated, and highest in an unsegmented market where the two firms have equal numbers of captives.

entry.title: Trade-offs between communication and privacy in distributed storage using shared secret keys
entry.summary: Communication and Privacy Trade-Offs in Distributed Storage With Shared Secret Keys arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies distributed storage in which all transmissions occur over a public channel, with privacy provided by shared secret keys. A user stores a file across L servers so that any t servers can reconstruct it, while any z colluding servers learn at most a fraction α of the file. For a fixed key length n, the authors characterize the trade-off between the privacy leakage α and the maximum securely storable file size. They also determine the minimum local randomness, public communication, and storage needed to achieve this optimal trade-off.

entry.title: Generative rate-distortion-perception theory on Riemannian manifolds: how much information is needed for generated outputs to stay accurate on curved spaces.
entry.summary: Generative Rate-Distortion-Perception Theory on Riemannian Manifolds arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper studies how much source information must be sent so that a receiver's generated outputs meet fidelity and reliability requirements on compact Riemannian manifolds, while preserving the source distribution. It proposes a generative rate-distortion-perception framework without common randomness and gives a single-letter characterization of the asymptotic operational function. For uniform sources on compact homogeneous manifolds, geometric lower and upper bounds coincide, giving an exact limiting result. On unit spheres, it shows that for dimension d≥2, adding d bits per source symbol can reduce the distortion radius by more than half.

entry.title: DistOptimize: Automatic Optimizer for Distributed Protocols
entry.summary: DistOptimize: Automatic Optimization of Distributed Protocols arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper presents DistOptimize, an automatic optimizer for distributed protocols that avoids safety risks from manual changes. It adapts throughput optimizations from academic languages to production frameworks, verifies the rewrites' correctness in Rocq, and automates their application using calibration and ILP-based search. Applied to fundamental protocols and protocols used at AWS, it improves throughput by up to 4x while increasing latency by at most 0.3ms.

entry.title: RARE: A new equilibrium for pricing games where sellers can respond to price changes
entry.summary: RARE: Response-Aware Rational Equilibrium in Pricing Games arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies pricing games in markets where budget-constrained buyers choose utility-maximizing bundles and each seller sets a price for one good. It proposes Response-Aware Rational Equilibrium (RARE), in which any seller's deviation can be deterred by other sellers' responses, and shows that RARE exists under certain conditions, with approximate versions for some cases. The authors also analyze a price-raising dynamic that reaches an approximate RARE.

entry.title: Principal-agent hypothesis testing with adaptive, sequential experimentation
entry.summary: Principal-agent hypothesis testing under adaptive experimentation arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies principal-agent hypothesis testing, where a principal rewards an agent based on data the agent generates. It extends the single-shot framework to sequential settings, where evidence accumulates over time, rewards may be deferred or paid incrementally, and the agent can stop the contract at a strategically chosen time. The main result shows that such contracts, called null-deterring, are characterized by e-processes.

entry.title: Random Non-Commutative Error-Correcting Codes: Extending Random Coding Theory to Arbitrary Groups
entry.summary: Random Non-Commutative Error-Correcting Codes arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper builds on the non-commutative error-correcting codes introduced by Chapman, Dinur, and Lubotzky, studying random codes over arbitrary groups as an analogue of classical random coding. It examines how far the classical Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound extends to this setting, showing that random universal codes of linear size in free groups are asymptotically bad. The authors characterize exactly which families of finite groups admit good random codes, namely those with uniform polynomial maximal-subgroup growth. They also give explicit quantitative bounds on rate and optimal distance based on intrinsic group parameters, and prove that families of finite solvable groups always form GV families.

entry.title: Slant: Deliberately Uneven Traffic Routing to Save Resources in Microservices
entry.summary: Slant: Shaping Traffic for Resource-Efficient Microservices arXiv · Oct 29, 2026Load balancers in microservice systems usually aim for even request distribution without considering how routing affects autoscaling signals and resource efficiency. This paper presents Slant, a resource-aware load balancing framework that intentionally creates safe traffic imbalance to improve utilization and works with existing vertical pod autoscalers without modification. In experiments on three microservice benchmarks, Slant reduces allocated CPU cores by up to 26% and lowers P99 latency by up to 18% compared to Round-Robin.

entry.title: A paper on a unified system for managing data, metadata and paradata of 3D digital cultural heritage objects, covering automated workflows, federated login and publishing.
entry.summary: Integrated data, metadata, and paradata management system for 3D Digital Cultural Heritage objects: Workflow automation, federated authentication, and publication arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper addresses the difficulty of managing complex, high-quality 3D digitised cultural heritage objects and their interconnected metadata. It proposes a global federated authentication and authorisation mechanism, a data and metadata management system, and an integrated engine for designing and running automated workflows. The solution is evaluated on three distinct 3D digitised cultural objects, showing the full process from data upload to publication.

entry.title: Dimension-free exponential entropy quotients over the field F₂
entry.summary: Dimension-free exponential entropy quotients over 𝔽₂ arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies entropy quotients for random vectors over F₂. For every ε>0, the authors show there is a subspace G with dimension at most 2^{320(1+ε)/ε} times H(X) such that H(q_GX) is at most (1+ε)(H(q_GX+q_GX')−H(q_GX)). The coefficient does not depend on the ambient dimension, and its exponential order in 1/ε is shown to be necessary.

entry.title: Determining the weight enumerators of binary extremal self-dual codes of length 60
entry.summary: Determination of weight enumerators of binary extremal self-dual codes of length 60 arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper constructs three binary extremal self-dual codes of length 60 whose weight enumerators were not previously known to occur. This completes the determination of all weight enumerators that arise for binary extremal self-dual codes of length 60.

entry.title: Random Centres and the ε-Dependence of Constant-Round Planar Domination
entry.summary: Random Centres and the ǎrepsilon-Dependence of Constant-Round Planar Domination arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies constant-round LOCAL algorithms for minimum dominating set on planar graphs. It replaces the heaviest-edge star selection in the clustering step with a random-centre rule, which reduces the round-complexity exponent. The authors also analyse how the approximation parameter ε affects the number of rounds, showing Ω(1/ε) rounds are needed on paths and Θ(1/ε) rounds are optimal on forests and outerplanar graphs. ★★★★ Notable: Replaces heaviest-edge star selection with random centres, reducing the planar round exponent from about 25.81 to below 5.89, with lower bounds reported.

entry.title: Simultaneous Gradient Learning in First-Price Auctions: How Gradient-Based Learning Converges to Equilibrium Under Private Information
entry.summary: Simultaneous Gradient Learning in First-Price Auctions arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper uses first-price auctions as a testbed to study equilibrium learning in discretized Bayesian games. It introduces Bayesian semicoarse correlated equilibrium (BSCCE), a refinement of Bayesian coarse correlated equilibrium (BCCE), and gives a linear programming characterization. The main finding is that the BSCCE set contracts in many cases as the discretization is refined, with its polytope diameter shrinking toward zero and converging to the unique continuous-game Bayes-Nash equilibrium.

entry.title: Hybrid multiple access for uplink communication using atomic quantum receivers to reduce transmit power
entry.summary: Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receiver Empowered Hybrid Non-orthogonal Multiple Access arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes an uplink hybrid NOMA architecture assisted by Rydberg atomic quantum receivers to improve energy efficiency. It formulates a joint optimization of phase measurements and multi-user power allocation to minimize total transmit power, solved with a three-layer hierarchical decomposition framework. Simulations report about a 93% reduction in total power consumption compared with OMA baselines while maintaining backward compatibility.

entry.title: A π/4 lower bound on recovery time for random access in symmetric linear codes
entry.summary: A π / 4 lower bound for random access in symmetric linear ensembles under optimal decoding arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper studies how many random linear observations are expected before a specific information symbol can be recovered. For ensembles with uniformly random supports, independent nonzero coefficients, and bounded column weights, it proves that the asymptotic normalized expected recovery time is at least π/4 under optimal decoding. The bound holds over finite or infinite fields and extends an earlier result for binary fully symmetric codes under peeling decoding.

entry.title: MacKay-Neal Codes for DNA Channels Under Block-MAP Decoding
entry.summary: MacKay-Neal Codes for DNA Channels under Block-MAP Decoding arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies MacKay-Neal socket codes for a quaternary insertion-deletion-substitution channel that models DNA reads, decoded with block maximum a posteriori (MAP) decoding. It proves that for a family of fixed-degree socket ensembles, the limiting rate is 6/ℓ bits per nucleotide, and that the ensemble-average block error is O(1/n) when the joint symmetric information rate of a fixed number of reads exceeds this rate. Deterministic graph-offset sequences are shown to achieve the same limiting rate and error bound.

entry.title: Polynomial-time constructions of asymptotically good random access codes
entry.summary: Polynomial-Time Constructions of Asymptotically Good Random Access Codes from Linear Codes arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Random access codes compress a q-ary input string into fewer q-ary symbols so that any requested input symbol can be recovered with probability above the random-guessing level 1/q. The paper introduces asymptotically good RACs and gives two polynomial-time constructions: OA-RACs built from linear codes via their orthogonal-array property, and a direct-sum strategy using q-ary Hamming codes that yields asymptotically good families at every rate in (0,1). Numerical results show favorable finite-length performance for both constructions.

entry.title: Is dual polarization always optimal? A study of new spatial degrees of freedom
entry.summary: Is Dual Polarization Always Optimal? Unlocking New Spatial Degrees of Freedom arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents a modular, low-cost tripolarized antenna operating in the 2.4 GHz band to experimentally test theoretical findings about tripolarized antennas. Experiments were conducted in two indoor scenarios and one outdoor scenario, with a multi-antenna transmitter and a receiver using a single tripolarized antenna. The authors report that this antenna can increase the number of spatial streams up to three or extend the region where terminals achieve two spatial streams.

entry.title: FlatCake: A flat storage design for reusing LLM attention caches across host memory and SSD
entry.summary: FlatCake: A Flat KVCache Storage Architecture for LLM Serving arXiv · Oct 28, 2026FlatCake is a storage architecture for LLM serving that treats host DRAM and NVMe SSD as equal peer media in one unified address space, instead of a tiered cache. Each KV block is placed at creation directly on its target medium in session-contiguous, layer-major order and is never moved. On a production Claude Code trace, the authors report a 94% cache hit rate under increasing load (versus 64% for Mooncake) and a 1.6× reduction in peak-load mean TTFT.

entry.title: Exact second-order asymptotics for the Gaussian Gray-Wyner problem
entry.summary: Exact Second-Order Asymptotics for the Gaussian Gray--Wyner Problem arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper revisits the Gray-Wyner problem of lossy compression for bivariate Gaussian sources under quadratic distortion and derives exact second-order asymptotics. It first identifies boundary rate tuples using the explicit first-order results of Yu (TIT 2023), then characterizes the tradeoff among three second-order coding rates under a joint excess-distortion probability constraint. The main contribution is an achievability proof based on a covariance shell covering lemma, analogous to the type covering lemma for discrete sources, and the asymptotic analysis is completed using the Berry-Esseen theorem.

entry.title: Understanding the Value of Anarchy: Empirical Studies of Best Response Dynamics
entry.summary: Toward Understanding the Value of Anarchy: Empirical Studies on Best Response Dynamics arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper experimentally tests best response dynamics (BRD) on randomly generated weighted networked multiagent optimization problems, comparing results with the Price of Anarchy (PoA) and with randomly selecting an equilibrium. The results show that simple best response mechanics tend to outperform both the PoA prediction and uniform random equilibrium selection, even when agents cannot observe all other agents' actions. The study also finds that when multiple equilibria exist, BRD appears biased toward higher-performing ones.

entry.title: A comparative study of parallel short-time Fourier transform implementations
entry.summary: A Comparative Study of Parallel Implementations of Short-Time Fourier Transform arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper compares two parallel algorithms for the short-time Fourier transform (STFT), which shows how a signal's frequencies change over time. One is FFT-based and the other is a quasi-parallel feedforward algorithm. Each is tested with shared-memory, distributed-memory, and hybrid parallel approaches, and the study analyzes runtime, memory use, and communication cost.

entry.title: Improved Johnson Bound for List-Decoding with Hints
entry.summary: An Improved Johnson Bound for List-Decoding with Hints arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies whether list-decoding radius for error-correcting codes can exceed the classical Johnson radius when some nearby codewords, called hints, are known. It determines the optimal list-decoding radius for single and multiple hints and shows it equals the optimum of a natural convex program. The authors also give an efficient weighted Guruswami-Sudan based algorithm that list-decodes Reed-Solomon codes up to this optimal radius.

entry.title: Lower bounds on b-symbol weights of dual Melas codes and a Poisson randomness postulate
entry.summary: On the b-Symbol Weight Distribution of Dual Melas Codes and a Poisson Randomness Postulate arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proves a new lower bound on the b-symbol weight of codewords in dual Melas codes that is strictly better than known results. It recasts a pattern counting problem in linear-feedback shift register sequences as a problem about orbits of binary polynomials under a certain action. The same techniques yield an improved burst-covering radius bound for Melas codes and a new upper bound on the critical exponent of dual Melas codes. The authors also define a randomness postulate for binary sequences based on infinite Poisson generic sequences, conjecture that dual Melas codewords satisfy it, and report partial progress.

entry.title: A Poisson transition and bias law for KSG mutual-information estimation
entry.summary: A Poisson Transition and Bias Law for KSG Mutual-Information Estimation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies the error of the KSG-1 mutual-information estimator on a Gaussian channel as sample size grows and the channel becomes nearly deterministic. The authors define a resolution parameter u_n = n·e^(-I_n) and prove that, when it converges to a positive limit, the estimation error converges in mean square to a computable deterministic bias. The bias is derived from an explicit marked-Poisson law for neighborhood counts, which also gives the limiting saturation probability.

entry.title: Joint Trajectory and Resource Optimization for Secure UAV Networks Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: Efficient Joint Trajectory Optimization and Resource Allocation for Secure UAV Networks: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how to jointly optimize UAV trajectories and resource allocation in wireless networks where a tethered UAV flying center and a malicious ground eavesdropper are present. The UAVs harvest energy and adaptively switch between transmitting, jamming, and relaying roles to deliver data to the tethered center. The authors formulate a utility maximization problem that balances secrecy rate, energy consumption, and interference, and solve it with a Proximal Policy Optimization based deep reinforcement learning algorithm. Simulations show better secrecy performance, lower energy use, and reduced interference than conventional and other DRL-based methods.

entry.title: ConfluxServe: Balancing Resource Use and Parallel Efficiency in LLM Prefill and Decode
entry.summary: ConfluxServe: Reconciling Resource Utilization and Parallelism Efficiency across Prefill and Decode in LLM Serving arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Prefill and decode use resources in complementary ways but prefer different parallelism strategies. The paper proposes Conflux Parallelism, which runs both phases in the same batch with different parallelism across operators. Building on this, it presents ConfluxServe, an SLO-aware serving system that maximizes goodput under TTFT and TBT constraints. On production workloads, it improves serving goodput by 1.26 to 1.62 times over the strongest baselines.

entry.title: Interference-Conjugate Transform: A Tightest Surrogate for Wireless Power Control, Scheduling and Beamforming
entry.summary: The Interference-Conjugate Transform: The Tightest Interference-Linear Surrogate for Power Control, Scheduling and Beamforming in Wireless Networks arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper proposes the interference-conjugate transform (ICT) for maximizing weighted sum rate in wireless networks. It proves that ICT is the unique best member of the family of interference-linear surrogates that includes FP, WMMSE, SEFP and XMMSE, and is pointwise dominant over these benchmarks. In uplink scheduling experiments, ICT achieves higher proportional-fairness utility than FP and SEFP using fewer iterations per slot, and in multi-cell MISO beamforming it converges in fewer iterations than the benchmarks.

entry.title: Pooled testing under congestion: scaling laws for choosing pool sizes
entry.summary: Pooled Testing under Congestion: Operational Scaling Laws for Pool-Size Selection arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper models pooled testing with random sample arrivals and limited testing capacity as a queueing system. It derives exact performance formulas and asymptotic scaling laws for fixed-batch Dorfman testing and a dynamic two-threshold policy. The optimal pool size depends jointly on prevalence, capacity, and delay, following a square-root law, a cube-root law, or remaining bounded depending on the regime.

entry.title: Minimum subpacketization of Reed-Solomon codes for cut-set-optimal linear repair
entry.summary: The Minimum Subpacketization of Reed-Solomon Codes with Linear Repair Achieving the Cut-Set Bound arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies the smallest subpacketization of Reed-Solomon codes that allow exact linear repair of every coordinate from any d helpers while meeting the cut-set bound. It proves a lower bound of sG_s(d+1) and shows it equals sG_s(n) when d(d+2) ≥ 4(n+1). The paper also gives a finite formula for G_s(n), an asymptotic growth result, and an affine-plane example showing sG_s(n) is not universal, along with a conjecture. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show a lower bound sG_s(d+1) on the minimum subpacketization of RS codes with exact linear repair, and state that for d(d+2)≥4(n+1) it equals sG_s(n), covering full-helper repair for distr

entry.title: Adapting hybrid LLM inference to each request for greater efficiency
entry.summary: Request-Adaptive Execution for Efficient Hybrid LLM Inference arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents Morph, a serving system that co-designs model architecture and runtime so hybrid language models can choose their layer layout per request. Each block pairs Attention and state space model layers, and a prefill-stage gate selects a layout that stays fixed during decoding. Experiments on six datasets report a better quality-efficiency trade-off than static hybrid baselines, with serving throughput improved by up to 3.87x and substantially lower inference latency.

entry.title: Privacy-preserving over-the-air federated learning in cell-free massive MIMO with user-centric clustering
entry.summary: Privacy-Preserving Over-the-Air Federated Learning over Cell-Free Massive MIMO System with User-Centric Clustering arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies a cross-layer design for differentially private federated learning over cell-free massive MIMO networks, where user model updates are aggregated over the air. It shows that thermal noise in wireless reception can help mask private information, reducing or removing the need for artificial noise. The authors jointly optimize access point-user associations, transmit powers, and artificial noise variances to minimize aggregation variance under per-user privacy constraints. Simulations report up to 89% lower aggregation variance than baselines and 97% test accuracy on MNIST, with consistent gains on CIFAR-10.

entry.title: Capacity of private information retrieval from coded storage with colluding, robust and Byzantine servers
entry.summary: The Capacity of Private Information Retrieval from Coded Storage Systems with Colluding, Robust and Byzantine Servers arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies private information retrieval from MDS-coded databases that include T colluding servers, U robust servers, and B Byzantine servers. The authors characterize the capacity for linear, full support-rank schemes and show the same expression holds without those restrictions when K=1 or T=1. They also extend the construction to retrieving P out of M files, and report that for P≥M/2 with K=1 or T=1 the multi-file scheme achieves capacity.

entry.title: Uniqueness of codes for 4-cell connected disjoint clusters in the spatial chromatic model
entry.summary: Code uniqueness of 4-cell connected disjoint clusters in spatial chromatic model arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies the coding of the spatial chromatic model (SCM), an entity-oriented spatial data model in which each cell has a chromatic code. Earlier work had shown uniqueness for 2-cell and 3-cell connected disjoint clusters. Building on that, the authors prove that the chromatic codes of 4-cell connected disjoint clusters are unique.

entry.title: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM Agent Serving
entry.summary: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents TAO, a scheduling framework for serving LLM-based agents that alternate between GPU model inference and external tools running on CPUs. TAO's value function combines near-term tool readiness, node-specific cache credit with time-aware decay, and token footprint, and a dynamic program jointly selects and places waiting sessions under capacity limits. Across 12 reported model-workload-concurrency settings, TAO reduces latency by up to 26.8%, mean time to first token by up to 36.3%, and increases decode throughput by up to 29.5% relative to the best evaluated baseline for each metric.

entry.title: PipeLink: Contract-Guided Linking of GPU Kernel Components
entry.summary: PipeLink: Contract-Guided Linking of GPU Kernel Components arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents PipeLink, a linker that combines separately compiled GPU kernel components using contracts stating what each component requires and provides. PipeLink checks these contracts, solves a joint placement of streaming multiprocessor resources, and generates the transfers between components. Across 51 configurations on Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, linked kernels run within 0.2% of the same sources compiled as one unit. ★★★★ Notable: PipeLink links separately compiled GPU kernel components via contracts stating their requirements and promises, solving one joint placement of SM resources and generating inter-component transfers. Th

entry.title: Negative Results for Over-the-Air Split Learning Under Channel Aging
entry.summary: Negative Results for Reciprocity-Based Over-the-Air Split Learning Under Channel Aging: Stability, Alignment, and Geometry arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies reciprocity-based over-the-air split learning, where channel aging rotates and attenuates the derivative signal sent back to the transmitter. Seven case studies combine numerical forecasts, mechanism checks, and competing predictions. Most predicted training accuracy gains are not supported, while some local physical relations, such as the inverse relation between amplitude and phase gradient, hold.

entry.title: Deep Holes and Aperture: Sign Laws for Lattice-Sampled Random Waves
entry.summary: Deep Holes and Aperture: Sign Laws for the Empirical Correlation of Lattice-Sampled Random Wave Fields arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies whether the empirical lag correlation of a Gaussian random wave field, sampled on a lattice within a bounded aperture, keeps a positive real part throughout the Voronoi cell. It identifies deep holes as the minimizers that govern failure and gives explicit sign-class counts for square, hexagonal, simple cubic, and body-centered cubic lattices. The authors also derive asymptotic and non-asymptotic aperture laws and state when a failure floor appears under Rayleigh-faded specular paths.

entry.title: Counting the fixed points of binary belief propagation: generic degree, syzygies, and real solutions
entry.summary: Counting the Fixed Points of Binary Belief Propagation: Generic Degree, Syzygies, and Real Solutions arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper studies how many fixed points belief propagation has on a binary pairwise model. Over complex parameters, it determines the generic degree of the algebraic family arising from finite loopless multigraphs, expressed as a graph state sum over edge sets without degree-one vertices. Two geometric realizations of this state sum are given, and at strong external fields the real fixed point count is analyzed as a lower bound. The degree, resolution, and real-count results are formalized in Lean 4.

entry.title: Wireless localization using digital twins and probabilistic inverse learning
entry.summary: Digital Twin-Guided Wireless Localization via Probabilistic Inverse Learning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how site-specific digital twins can support wireless localization with simplified distributed infrastructure. It proposes PRISM, a probabilistic scheme using single-antenna access points, which learns a proposal distribution over user locations from channel impulse responses and reweights candidates using digital twin consistency. With 10 single-antenna access points, it reports a median error of about 0.7 m and remains effective without retraining when digital twin features are degraded.

entry.title: Contention-aware scheduling to handle skewed sparse matrix multiplication (technical report)
entry.summary: Taming Multi-Dimensional Skew in Sparse Matrix Multiplication with Contention-Aware Scheduling [Technical Report] arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This report examines why sparse matrix-matrix multiplication (SpGEMM) slows down on skewed real-world workloads. It identifies two causes: imbalance across computation cost, output density, and data locality, and cache contention from dense substructures. The authors propose adaptive morsel scheduling (AMS), which combines contention-aware load balancing, a data-conscious SMT activator, and a per-morsel hybrid accumulator. Evaluations on matrix squaring, relational queries, and graph analytics report that AMS significantly outperforms existing methods on skewed workloads while staying comparable on non-skewed ones.

entry.title: Physics-informed neural operator for channel estimation in fluid antenna systems
entry.summary: Rethinking Channel Estimation for Fluid Antenna Systems: A Physics-Informed Operator Learning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper frames channel estimation for fluid antenna systems as a stochastic inverse field-reconstruction problem constrained by the projected Helmholtz model. It shows that finite-aperture reconstruction leads to a frequency-domain deconvolution problem and proposes a U-shaped Fourier neural operator trained with a physics-aware Sobolev loss. Simulations report higher accuracy than state-of-the-art benchmarks and much lower inference latency than iterative solvers at high spatial-frequency resolutions.

entry.title: How the power delay profile threshold affects RMS delay spread estimates at 33 GHz
entry.summary: Sensitivity of RMS Delay Spread Estimation to Power Delay Profile Thresholding in Time-Varying Channels at 33 GHz arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines how estimates of RMS delay spread, a measure of signal time dispersion in radio channels, change with the relative power threshold applied to power delay profiles. The analysis uses wideband measurements at 33 GHz in a dynamic road environment with moving vehicles. Lowering the threshold from -20 dB to -50 dB raises the median from about 140 ns to 168 ns and the 90th percentile from 200 ns to 210 ns. Both statistics converge at lower thresholds, with -40 dB a practical convergence level.

entry.title: When Do Token Systems Stabilize? Compatibility Constraints and Community Structure
entry.summary: When do token systems stabilize? Compatibility constraints and community structure arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies token systems that enable service exchange without money, where agents face compatibility constraints. It establishes a necessary and sufficient condition for stability and shows that a minimum-token rule, selecting the lowest-balance available provider, achieves the optimal stability region. The criterion is applied to random token systems generated by stochastic block models, identifying two obstructions to stability: insufficient service opportunities for a group of communities or for an individual agent.

entry.title: Finite Fields: root sets, Frobenius maps and algebraic structure (monograph)
entry.summary: Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality and cyclic modules. It applies these tools to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory, covering cyclic and constacyclic codes, BCH and Goppa bounds, rank-metric and trace codes. It also treats character sums, Gauss and Jacobi sums, and proofs of Weil bounds, emphasizing explicit links between field, orbit and linear-dependence structure.

entry.title: Characterizing Maximum Nash Welfare: Envy-Freeness and Proportionality
entry.summary: Characterizing Maximum Nash Welfare: Envy-Freeness and Proportionality arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how to allocate indivisible goods using the maximum Nash welfare rule. This rule was already known to be the only welfarist rule satisfying envy-freeness up to one good. The authors show that this fairness requirement can be replaced by much weaker conditions for any fixed k: envy-freeness up to k goods, or proportionality up to k goods. The characterization also holds for preference profiles with identical goods.

entry.title: Exact weight spectrum of RM(m-7,m): a counterexample to the Carlet-Solé conjecture
entry.summary: The Exact Weight Spectrum of RM(m-7,m): A Counterexample to the Carlet-Solé Conjecture arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies the weight spectrum of the Reed-Muller code RM(m-7,m), which describes which weights occur among Boolean functions of degree at most m-7. Combining affine geometry and Fourier analysis, the authors exclude eight weights previously conjectured for RM(7,14). They extend these exclusions to all m≥14 and thereby provide a counterexample to the Carlet-Solé conjecture.

entry.title: A new MIMO design using movable antennas that keeps signal paths strong
entry.summary: Design of DoF-Robust MIMO via Generalized Pinching Antennas arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines how distance differences between users and a base station can cause multi-user MIMO channels to lose spatial degrees of freedom. It proposes generalized pinching antennas placed close to users, which make the channel Gram matrix nearly diagonal and well-conditioned. Performance is assessed using rank-deficiency and outage probabilities. The analytical and simulation results indicate that pinching antennas can preserve spatial degrees of freedom and support users at spatially separated locations.

entry.title: Agar: What-If Analysis for Microservice Applications
entry.summary: Agar: What-If Analysis for Microservice Applications arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents AGAR, a counterfactual performance analysis tool for microservice applications. Instead of predicting exact values for each component, it learns simple, interpretable bounds that contain all observed behaviors and are tight enough to support end-to-end conclusions, then composes them to answer SLO-feasibility questions. This framing turns autoscaling into the query of finding the smallest resource allocation that meets an SLO. Across three microservice applications, the derived autoscaler reduces CPU allocation by up to 36.8% compared with state-of-the-art horizontal autoscalers while satisfying application SLOs.

entry.title: Noise Shapes the Surplus: Strategic Play Against No-Regret Learners
entry.summary: Noise Shapes the Surplus: Strategic Play Against No-Regret Learners arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how an optimizer in zero-sum games can gain cumulative payoff above the minimax benchmark against no-regret learners, here Follow-the-Regularized-Leader algorithms, that act on noisy payoff scores with decaying learning rates. Passive play earns at most constant surplus, while a clairvoyant optimizer secures surplus scaling with the inverse learning rate when the mean response is profitable. Active alternating play can still extract surplus from the learner's movement when it is not, and at the canonical rate the noiseless Ω(√T) surplus is recovered under mean-zero, finite-variance perturbations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that in zero-sum games, optimizers can still extract strategic surplus from noisy FTRL learners with decaying rates, including Ω(1/η_T) and Ω(∑η_t) results and an Ω(√T) rate at η_t∝

entry.title: Optimal and Impossible Strategyproof Facility Placement in Multiple Dimensions
entry.summary: Optimality and Impossibility in Multidimensional Strategyproof Facility Location arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies facility location in multidimensional normed spaces, aiming to minimize social cost, the sum of agents' distances to their nearest facility. For a single facility in the Euclidean plane, it shows that the optimal approximation ratios of deterministic strategyproof mechanisms match those of the coordinate-wise median, without assuming anonymity. It also shows that the coordinate-wise median is not always optimal in non-Euclidean spaces, and proves impossibility results for two or more facilities.

entry.title: Learning-Augmented Coordination Mechanisms: Using Demand Predictions to Improve Equilibrium Efficiency in Congestion Games
entry.summary: Learning-Augmented Coordination Mechanisms arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how selfish behavior reduces efficiency in decentralized resource allocation. It proposes learning-augmented coordination mechanisms that use a possibly inaccurate demand prediction to modify resource costs, with a confidence parameter β that yields near-optimal performance when predictions are accurate while keeping a good worst-case equilibrium guarantee. The paper also gives robustness bounds and impossibility results, including limits on error tolerance in non-atomic games. ★★★★ Notable: Introduces learning-augmented coordination mechanisms for congestion games, aiming for near-optimal performance under accurate predictions while retaining PoS guarantees, with impossibility results.

entry.title: JustGoal: An AI Given Only a Goal Beats Expert-Written GPU Kernels
entry.summary: JustGoal: With Only a Goal, the AI Baseline Is Above the Expert Kernels arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper introduces JustGoal, a baseline in which a general-purpose AI agent receives only an optimization goal and constraints, without kernel-specific knowledge bases or predefined workflows. On NVIDIA B200 GPUs, it beats open-source libraries on 8 of 10 operators, with per-operator geometric mean speedups of 1.14x to 2.34x, and beats the fastest public specialized-agent kernel on 5 of 9 comparable operators. The authors conclude that specialized machinery should be justified by clear gains over a same-model, goal-only baseline and reevaluated when the foundation model changes.

entry.title: Fundamental limits of bistatic ISAC over vector channels, i.e., the best achievable trade-off between communication rate and sensing accuracy.
entry.summary: On the Fundamental Limits of Bistatic ISAC Over Vector Channels arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies the fundamental performance limits of bistatic integrated sensing and communication systems over vector channels.
